name: Frieze–Kannan weak regularity
text: every graphon is within ε in cut norm of its block average over a measurable partition with at most 4^(⌈1/ε²⌉+1) parts (Frieze–Kannan 1999; Lovász, *Large Networks and Graph Limits*, §9.2) — the exponential bound that trades Szemerédi's tower for a weaker approximation.

name: The uniqueness half of Gabriel's theorem
text: over a quiver with positive definite Tits form, a finite-dimensional indecomposable representation is determined up to isomorphism by its dimension vector, by the Bernstein–Gelfand–Ponomarev reflection induction; the existence half, that every positive root is so realized, is separate later work.

name: Freudenthal's multiplicity formula
text: on a finite-dimensional highest weight module of weight λ over a Killing-semisimple Lie algebra, (⟨λ+ρ, λ+ρ⟩ − ⟨μ+ρ, μ+ρ⟩)·dim M_μ = 2 Σ_{α>0} Σ_{j≥1} dim M_{μ+jα}·⟨μ+jα, α⟩ (Humphreys, GTM 9, §22.3), and the left coefficient is nonzero for μ ≠ λ, so the recursion computes every weight multiplicity downward from dim M_λ = 1.

name: Goodman's inequality for graphons
text: the triangle density of a graphon is at least 2d² − d in its edge density d (Goodman 1959), whence Mantel's bound: a graphon with zero triangle density has edge density at most 1/2.

name: Finite-group representations are determined by their characters
text: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, two finite-dimensional representations of a finite group with equal characters are isomorphic, and the character map on the representation ring R(G) is injective (Serre, *Linear Representations of Finite Groups*, §2.3); Mathlib has the forward direction and the orthogonality relations, and this is the converse.

name: Integral closure in a purely inseparable extension is finite
text: the integral closure of k[X₁, …, Xᵣ] in a finite purely inseparable extension of its fraction field is a finite module (Stacks 032O); Mathlib's finiteness theorem argues through the trace pairing and so covers the separable case, and this is the inseparable half of normalization finiteness.

name: The Kostant partition function inverts the Weyl denominator
text: Σ_{T ⊆ Φ⁺} (−1)^|T| P(ν − Σ_{α∈T} α) = δ_{ν,0}, the coefficientwise form of Δ · Σ_ν P(ν) e^{−ν} = 1 (Kostant 1959), the combinatorial input to the Kostant multiplicity and Weyl character formulas.

name: An arithmetic Frobenius raises roots of unity to the norm of the prime below
text: for ζ an m-th root of unity in an extension of a number field and 𝔭 a prime of the base not dividing m, every arithmetic Frobenius at a prime above 𝔭 sends ζ to ζ^𝔑𝔭 (Washington, *Introduction to Cyclotomic Fields*, Ch. 1), so the mod-m cyclotomic character reads Frob_p ↦ p mod m.

name: Miyake's coprime-index filter
text: for a cusp form f ∈ S_k(Γ₁(N), χ) and squarefree L whose primes all divide N, some cusp form of level LN has the q-expansion of f restricted to the indices coprime to L (Miyake, *Modular Forms*, Lemma 4.6.5), the root of the descent tower toward strong multiplicity one.

name: Student's t distribution
text: the measure with density Γ((ν+1)/2)/(√(νπ) Γ(ν/2)) · (1 + x²/ν)^(−(ν+1)/2), proved a probability measure via Euler's second beta integral ∫₀^∞ x^(a−1)(1+x)^(−a−b) dx = Β(a,b), itself new here, with one degree of freedom recovering the Cauchy law.

name: The Artin symbol of an unramified prime
text: the conjugacy-class-valued Frobenius of a prime of a number field unramified in a finite Galois extension, well defined because every arithmetic Frobenius at every prime above it represents the same class (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, I §9); it packages Mathlib's arithmetic-Frobenius theory into the symbol the Chebotarev density theorem is stated with.

name: The central character of a highest weight module
text: the algebra homomorphism χ_λ : Z(U(L)) → K by which the centre of the enveloping algebra acts on every highest weight vector of weight λ — the infinitesimal character (Humphreys, *BGG Category O*, §1.7) — taking the Casimir element to its eigenvalue; the Harish-Chandra isomorphism is separate later work.

name: The irreducible 𝔤𝔩ₙ-module of a dominant weight
text: for every dominant integral weight μ over a field of characteristic zero there is a finite-dimensional irreducible 𝔤𝔩ₙ-module L(μ) with highest weight μ, constructed as the irreducible quotient of the submodule generated by a realizing highest weight vector and identified with any irreducible carrying such a vector, and restriction to 𝔰𝔩ₙ stays irreducible over any characteristic-zero field since the identity matrix acts by Σᵢ μᵢ — the existence half that the highest weight theorem for 𝔤𝔩ₙ of TauCeti#5155 was still waiting on, completing the classification (Goodman–Wallach, GTM 255, §5.5).

name: The numerical Grothendieck quotients of the Ext-Euler pairing
text: K₀ modulo the radical of the Euler form: for two extension-closed subcategories on which the pairing χ(X, Y) = Σᵢ (−1)ⁱ dim Extⁱ(X, Y) is defined, it descends from the exact Grothendieck groups to left and right numerical quotients on which it is nondegenerate, computed on object classes by the Euler characteristic itself — the abstract form of the numerical Grothendieck group of Bridgeland, Ann. of Math. 166 (2007), §1.3.

name: Microbial valuations
text: a valuation is microbial when some convex subgroup of its value group has height-one quotient; rank-one valuations are microbial and trivial ones are not (Wedhorn, *Adic Spaces*, Def. 5.46(v)) — the condition through which analytic points of Spa(A, A⁺) acquire the height-one vertical generizations consumed by Wedhorn's Proposition 7.49(2).

name: Frobenius' theorem on real division algebras
text: a finite-dimensional division algebra with centre ℝ is ℝ-isomorphic to ℝ or to Hamilton's quaternions ℍ, whence every real Brauer class is trivial or the class of ℍ and the Brauer group of ℝ is ℤ/2 (Gille–Szamuely, *Central Simple Algebras and Galois Cohomology*).

name: Fundamental groups of real projective spaces
text: π₁(ℝPⁿ) is trivial for n = 0, infinite for n = 1 (ℝP¹ is a circle), and of order two for every n ≥ 2 via the double cover Sⁿ → ℝPⁿ, now assembled as one trichotomy covering all dimensions (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, §1.3).

name: A positive definite Tits form forces finite representation type
text: the finiteness half of Gabriel's theorem: a finite quiver whose Tits form is positive definite has only finitely many indecomposable finite-dimensional representations up to isomorphism, at most one per positive root, composing the dimension-vector facts behind the uniqueness half of TauCeti#5299; the existence half and the ADE classification remain (Gabriel, *Unzerlegbare Darstellungen I*, 1972).

name: Uniqueness in the Lévy–Khintchine representation of Bernstein functions
text: two triplets of killing coefficient, nonnegative drift, and Lévy measure representing the same Bernstein function on [0, ∞) coincide, upgrading the existence theorem of TauCeti#4483 to unique existence and completing the representation theorem (Schilling–Song–Vondraček, *Bernstein Functions*, Thm 3.2).

name: The level-lowering dichotomy for cusp forms
text: for l ∣ N and a Dirichlet character χ mod N, a periodic f : ℍ → ℂ whose rescaling f(l·) is a cusp form in S_k(N, χ) either has χ factoring through N/l with f itself a cusp form of level N/l and the lowered character, or is zero (Miyake, *Modular Forms*, Thm 4.6.4); ported clause-for-clause from Chris Birkbeck's AINTLIB.

name: The p-Wasserstein distance
text: the infimum over couplings π of μ and ν of the L^p-norm of the ground distance under π, with p = ∞ a case of the same definition; symmetry, the triangle inequality by gluing plus Minkowski, monotonicity in the exponent, and separation of probability measures on a Polish space are proved, opening the metric layer of the optimal-transport development (Villani, *Optimal Transport*, Ch. 6).

name: Supernatural numbers
text: formal products ∏ p^(e_p) with exponents in ℕ ∪ {∞}, carrying the divisibility complete lattice, primary decompositions, and the embedding of the positive naturals: the arithmetic in which orders and indices of profinite groups are counted (Ribes–Zalesskii, *Profinite Groups*, §2.3).

name: Differential graded algebras
text: a square-zero degree-one endomorphism of an internally ℤ-graded algebra obeying the graded Leibniz rule, with cycles a graded subalgebra, boundaries a homogeneous two-sided ideal, and the graded cohomology algebra as the quotient — the opening layer of the DG/A∞ development (Weibel, *An Introduction to Homological Algebra*).

name: The Auslander–Reiten translate
text: τ M = D(Tr M), the k-dual of the transpose of TauCeti#5217, proved independent of the chosen minimal projective presentation and vanishing on projectives; AR duality and the bijection between non-projective and non-injective indecomposables are still to come (Auslander–Reiten–Smalø, *Representation Theory of Artin Algebras*, IV).

name: Carathéodory's boundary extension theorem
text: the Riemann map of a Jordan domain extends to a homeomorphism of the closed disc onto the closure of the domain, proved through cluster sets and Janiszewski's separation theorem rather than the Schoenflies theorem (Pommerenke, *Boundary Behaviour of Conformal Maps*, Ch. 2).

name: The canonical Néron–Tate height

reference.text: Voyager, TauCeti#5600, TauCeti#5601, TauCeti#5612, TauCeti#5619, TauCeti#5636

text: ĥ(P) = lim 4⁻ⁿ h(2ⁿP)/2 on an elliptic curve, by Tate's telescoping limit, with bounded difference from the naïve height, the exact parallelogram law, ĥ(nP) = n²ĥ(P), ĥ ≥ 0, and — under Northcott finiteness — ĥ(P) = 0 exactly at the torsion points; the Néron–Tate pairing and regulator are the next milestones (Silverman, *AEC*, VIII §9).

name: The Euler product of the Dedekind zeta function
text: ζ_K(s) = ∏ (1 − N𝔭⁻ˢ)⁻¹ over the primes of 𝓞_K for Re s > 1, from a general analytic Euler product for absolutely convergent ideal-indexed Dirichlet series; the prime-ideal counterpart of Mathlib's Euler product for ζ(s) (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, Ch. VII).

name: Associativity of the elliptic formal group law
text: the chord addition series of a Weierstrass curve satisfies F(F(t₁,t₂),t₃) = F(t₁,F(t₂,t₃)) over every commutative ring, the last axiom of the commutative formal group law of Ê; registering Ê as an instance of Mathlib's abstract formal groups is a separate later step (Silverman, *AEC*, IV §1).

name: The Cartan map and the resolution theorem
text: the map K₀(proj R) → G₀(mod R) of Grothendieck groups is an isomorphism whenever every finitely generated R-module admits a finite resolution by finitely generated projectives, e.g. over a semisimple ring (Weibel, *The K-book*, II §6.2 and V §3).

name: The Gamma–Poisson mixture is negative binomial
text: a Poisson law whose intensity is itself Gamma-distributed is a negative binomial law (Johnson–Kemp–Kotz, *Univariate Discrete Distributions*, Ch. 6).

name: Squares of Gaussians are chi-squared
text: the sum of squares of a finite independent family of standard Gaussian variables has the χ² law with that many degrees of freedom (Johnson–Kotz–Balakrishnan, *Continuous Univariate Distributions*, vol. 1).

name: Borel subgroups
text: a Borel subgroup of a linear algebraic group scheme, in Hopf coordinates: a smooth, geometrically connected, geometrically solvable closed subgroup maximal among such, with the upper-triangular subgroup of GL₂ proved Borel over every field via Bruhat decomposition (Springer, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, §6.2).

name: Almost-split (Auslander–Reiten) sequences
text: the sequence 0 → τM → E → M → 0 as a short exact complex whose two maps are left and right almost split, with non-splitness, indecomposability of the ends and self-duality derived rather than assumed; the Auslander–Reiten existence theorem is a later target (Auslander–Reiten–Smalø, *Representation Theory of Artin Algebras*, V.1).

name: Fisher's F distribution
text: the F(m,n) law as a pushforward of the Beta law, with cumulative distribution function the regularized incomplete beta function at mx/(n + mx); density and moments are still to come (Johnson–Kotz–Balakrishnan, *Continuous Univariate Distributions*, vol. 2).

name: Burnside's vanishing theorem
text: for an irreducible complex character χ of a finite group and an element g whose conjugacy class has size coprime to the degree χ(1), either χ(g) = 0 or ‖χ(g)‖ = χ(1) — the arithmetic dichotomy behind Burnside's pᵃqᵇ theorem, whose remaining steps are separate (Isaacs, *Character Theory of Finite Groups*, Thm 3.8).

name: The Dirichlet spectrum of a divergence-form elliptic operator
text: for L u = −∂ⱼ(aⁱʲ ∂ᵢu) + bⁱ ∂ᵢu + c u with a coercive symmetric energy form on a bounded open Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ, the solution operator on L²(Ω) is compact and self-adjoint (Rellich–Kondrachov plus Lax–Milgram), every Dirichlet eigenvalue is positive with the explicit Poincaré lower bound for −Δ, eigenspaces are finite-dimensional, and the eigenfunctions span a dense subspace of L²(Ω); the ordered eigenvalue sequence and min–max are later steps (Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, §6.5).

name: The Néron–Tate pairing
text: the canonical height ĥ polarises to the symmetric bilinear pairing ⟨P, Q⟩ = (ĥ(P+Q) − ĥ(P) − ĥ(Q))/2 on the points of an elliptic curve, with ⟨P, P⟩ = ĥ(P) and the torsion in its kernel, descending to the Mordell–Weil group modulo torsion, where it is positive definite under Northcott finiteness and has a Gram matrix in any basis — the input to the regulator, which is the next step (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, VIII §9).

name: The flow of a globally Lipschitz vector field
text: a globally Lipschitz vector field on a Banach space has a unique solution through every point defined on all of ℝ, by one Picard iteration in a cosh-weighted function space, and the solutions assemble into a jointly continuous flow with the group law and two-sided exponential dependence on initial conditions, extending Mathlib's interval-local Picard–Lindelöf; the negative gradient flow of Morse theory is the intended consumer (Dieudonné, *Foundations of Modern Analysis*, Ch. X).

name: A regular level set of a Fredholm map is a manifold
text: the level set of a C^m Fredholm map between Banach spaces at a regular value carries a C^m manifold structure modelled on the kernel of the derivative, of dimension the Fredholm index — the moduli-space package of McDuff–Salamon, *J-holomorphic Curves and Symplectic Topology*, Appendix A.3, upgrading the implicit-function charts of the local normal form (TauCeti#3235) to a smooth atlas.

name: The Hecke multiplication table for Γ₀(N)
text: in the double-coset Hecke ring of Γ₀(N), Tₘ · Tₙ = Σ_{d ∣ gcd(m,n)} d · S_d · T_{mn/d²} for all nonzero m and n, deduced from the per-prime table by an induction on the gcd (Shimura, *Introduction to the Arithmetic Theory of Automorphic Functions*, Thm 3.24(3)).

name: The Galois theory of translations on an elliptic function field
text: for a finite subgroup Φ of the points of a Weierstrass curve, the function-field extension F(W)/F(W)^Φ is Galois of degree #Φ with the translations as its full automorphism group — the field-theoretic input to the dual isogeny (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, III.4.10) — via Artin's fixed-field theorem proved for any finite automorphism group with no finite-dimensionality hypothesis on the ambient extension.

name: Finitely supported measures are dense in Wasserstein space
text: on a Polish metric space and for 1 ≤ p < ∞, the finitely supported probability laws are dense in the Wasserstein space P_p(X), and the N-point quantization error of a fixed law tends to zero (Villani, *Optimal Transport: Old and New*; Graf–Luschgy, *Foundations of Quantization for Probability Distributions*).

name: Projective covers exist over a semiprimary ring
text: every module — with no finiteness hypothesis — over a semiprimary ring has a projective cover, the existence half joining the uniqueness announced with TauCeti#3266; semiperfect rings are defined alongside, with semiprimary rings semiperfect (Lam, *A First Course in Noncommutative Rings*, §23–24).

name: Galois orbits are the irreducible factors
text: the orbits of Gal(p) on the roots of a polynomial biject with its monic irreducible factors, a separable factor's degree counting the roots in its orbit; hence a separable polynomial of positive degree is irreducible exactly when the root action is transitive, sharpening Mathlib's irreducible-implies-transitive to an equivalence (Dummit–Foote, *Abstract Algebra*, Ch. 14).

name: An orthonormal basis of Dirichlet eigenfunctions
text: a compact symmetric operator on any Hilbert space has a Hilbert basis of eigenvectors, and applied to the solution operator of L u = −∂ⱼ(aⁱʲ ∂ᵢu) + bⁱ ∂ᵢu + c u on a bounded open Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ this gives L²(Ω) an orthonormal basis of Dirichlet eigenfunctions, with the solution expansion L⁻¹f = Σ κ⁻¹⟨eₖ, f⟩eₖ — upgrading the density of eigenfunctions announced with TauCeti#5632 (Reed–Simon, *Methods of Modern Mathematical Physics I*; Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, §6.5).

name: The Rayleigh characterisation of the first Dirichlet eigenvalue
text: for the same operators, κ₁ is the minimum of the Rayleigh quotient a(u, u)/‖u‖² over nonzero u ∈ H¹₀(Ω), ‖·‖ the L²(Ω) norm, equivalently the greatest constant in the Poincaré-type inequality C‖u‖² ≤ a(u, u), with the minimum attained via Rellich–Kondrachov (Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, §6.5).

name: Subgroups classify the pointed connected covers
text: every pointed connected cover of (X, x₀) is the quotient of the universal cover by a unique subgroup of π₁(X, x₀), so the parametrisation is a bijection under which unpointed isomorphism is conjugacy and regularity is normality (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Thm 1.38) — the subgroup form of the classification, beside the monodromy equivalence of categories announced earlier.

name: The complex Specht modules classify the irreducible representations of Sₙ
text: ℂ ⊗ S^μ is simple, distinct shapes give non-isomorphic modules, and every simple object of FDRep ℂ Sₙ arises for exactly one partition of n, so the irreducible complex characters of Sₙ are exactly the χ^μ — carrying the rational classification announced earlier across the base change, by absolute irreducibility and flatness of intertwiner spaces (James–Kerber, *The Representation Theory of the Symmetric Group*).

name: The degree of multiplication by n is n²
text: on an elliptic curve over any field the isogeny [n] has degree n² for every nonzero integer n, via the division-polynomial computation that x ∘ [n] = Φₙ/ΨSqₙ has degree n² as a rational map — the multiplication-by-n half of the degree theory the Hasse bound consumes (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, III.6.4(a)).

name: Sidorenko's inequality for the 4-cycle
text: every graphon W on a probability carrier satisfies t(C₄, W) ≥ t(K₂, W)⁴: the homomorphism density of the four-cycle is at least the fourth power of the edge density, the C₄ case of Sidorenko's conjecture, by the classical Cauchy–Schwarz argument (Lovász, *Large Networks and Graph Limits*).

name: The Frobenius generates the decomposition group
text: at a prime Q of a finite Galois extension of number fields, unramified over 𝔭 below, an arithmetic Frobenius induces the residue-field Frobenius, has order the inertia degree f(Q/𝔭), generates the decomposition group, and is conjugated along the fibre by the Galois action (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, I §9).

name: The Wasserstein space P_p(X) is complete and separable
text: for 1 ≤ p < ∞ the finite-moment Wasserstein space is separable when X is separable and complete when X is complete and separable, by the classical path-space gluing of near-optimal couplings, so P_p of a Polish space is Polish (Villani, *Optimal Transport: Old and New*, Thm 6.18).

name: Smooth dependence of an ODE solution on its initial condition
text: for x′ = v(x) with v of class C^(n+1) and globally Lipschitz, the solution is jointly C^(n+1) in initial condition and time near t = 0, packaged as a genuine local flow with the law Φ(x, t + s) = Φ(Φ(x, t), s) for a field smooth only near a point — the C^k dependence extending Mathlib's Lipschitz estimate, by a time rescaling that turns the initial condition into a parameter (Lang, *Differential and Riemannian Manifolds*).

name: The self-duality criterion for irreducible highest-weight modules
text: a finite-dimensional irreducible module of highest weight λ over a split semisimple Lie algebra carries a nonzero invariant bilinear form exactly when −(w₀ • λ) = λ for the longest Weyl element w₀, the dual being irreducible of highest weight −(w₀ • λ) (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*, §21.6; Bourbaki, *Groupes et algèbres de Lie*, VIII §7.5).

name: The regulator of an elliptic curve
text: the absolute determinant of the Gram matrix of the Néron–Tate pairing on a basis of the points modulo torsion, independent of the chosen basis, with Reg = 1 at rank zero — completing the canonical-height strand the pairing (TauCeti#5660) opened; positivity awaits positive-definiteness on the real span (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, VIII §9).

name: The geodesic spray
text: the vector field (x, v) ↦ (v, −Γₓ(v, v)) on the tangent bundle of a Riemannian manifold, whose integral curves are proved to be exactly the velocity lifts t ↦ (γ(t), γ′(t)) of geodesics — the object that feeds the exponential map and Hopf–Rinow, with smoothness of the spray itself the next step (do Carmo, *Riemannian Geometry*, Ch. 3).

name: Burnside's pᵃqᵇ theorem
text: a finite group of order pᵃqᵇ, for primes p and q, is solvable, by the classical character-theoretic route: a conjugacy class of prime-power size larger than one forces a proper nontrivial normal subgroup, which spends the vanishing theorem of TauCeti#5578, and an induction on the order with a Sylow argument finishes; this closes the milestone that bullet left open (Burnside 1904; Isaacs, *Character Theory of Finite Groups*, Thm 3.10).

name: Stone's theorem for unbounded self-adjoint operators
text: a densely defined self-adjoint operator A on a complex Hilbert space is the generator of exactly one strongly continuous unitary group e^{itA}, and an operator is self-adjoint exactly when iA generates such a group; this is the converse direction that the generator bullet of TauCeti#5185 left open, obtained by gluing the Lumer–Phillips contraction semigroups of iA and −iA into a group (Reed–Simon, *Methods of Modern Mathematical Physics I*, Thm VIII.8; Engel–Nagel, Thm II.3.24).

name: The strong exchange condition for Coxeter systems
text: in an arbitrary Coxeter system, if a reflection t shortens w then t·w is spelled by any word for w with one letter deleted, with the exchange and deletion conditions as corollaries and the inversion sequence of a reduced word listing exactly the inversions of its element; TauCeti#2823 had this for Weyl groups from the geometry of positive roots, and this is the general case by the reflection cocycle, with Matsumoto's theorem the next milestone (Björner–Brenti, *Combinatorics of Coxeter Groups*, §1.4; Humphreys §5.8).

name: The standard basis theorem for Specht modules
text: the polytabloids of the standard Young tableaux of shape μ form a basis of the Specht module S^μ over ℚ, so dim S^μ = f^μ, the number of standard tableaux of shape μ; linear independence is triangularity in the dominance order and spanning is the straightening algorithm through the Garnir relations (James, *The Representation Theory of the Symmetric Groups*, §8; Sagan, *The Symmetric Group*, Thm 2.5.2).

name: Gauss's 2-rank formula for quadratic fields of either signature
text: for K = ℚ(√d), d squarefree, real or imaginary, the 2-rank of the narrow class group Cl⁺(K) is exactly t − 1, t the number of ramified rational primes: the lower bound is the independence of the genus characters, every sign pattern of product one being realised by a degree-one prime from Dirichlet's theorem, and it closes the real case that the first-inequality bullet of TauCeti#4222 left open; the narrow ambiguous class number 2^(t−1) and |Gal(K_gen/K)| = |Cl⁺(K)/Cl⁺(K)²| for the narrow genus field follow (Lemmermeyer, *Reciprocity Laws*, §2.2; Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, §6.A).

name: The discriminant test for the alternating group
text: for a monic separable polynomial over a field of characteristic other than 2, the discriminant is a square in the base field exactly when the Galois group permutes the roots evenly, via σ(δ) = sign(σ)·δ for the root-difference product δ = ∏_{i<j}(rᵢ − rⱼ); in characteristic 2 every such discriminant is a square, so the test is vacuous there (Cohen, *A Course in Computational Algebraic Number Theory*, §6.3; Dummit–Foote §14.6).

name: The degree of a multiquadratic extension
text: over a field K of characteristic other than 2, adjoining square roots of units d₁, …, dₙ gives an extension of degree 2^r, r the 𝔽₂-rank of the subgroup of K^×/(K^×)² generated by the classes of the dᵢ, so each independent multiplicative relation among the radicands halves the degree; the exponent-two case of Kummer theory with no independence hypothesis, following Michael Stoll's QuadraticIterates formalisation (Lang, *Algebra*, VI §8).

name: The Herbrand quotient
text: h(M) = |Ĥ⁰(G, M)| / |Ĥ⁻¹(G, M)| on Mathlib's Tate cohomology, with Ĥ⁻¹(G, M) identified as ker N / I_G M, h(M) = 1 for a finite module over a finite cyclic group and h(ℤ) = |G| for the trivial integral representation; multiplicativity in short exact sequences is the next milestone (Serre, *Local Fields*, VIII §4).

name: Toric cones
text: the rational polyhedral cones of toric geometry as a predicate on a Mathlib pointed cone relative to a lattice map: generated by finitely many lattice vectors and containing no line, closed under faces, products and injective compatible linear maps, with a counterexample showing that intersections need not be toric when the lattice image is not discrete (Cox–Little–Schenck, *Toric Varieties*, §1.2; Fulton, *Introduction to Toric Varieties*, §1.2).

name: The special isogeny of Sp₄ in characteristic two
text: over any commutative ring R of characteristic 2, the endomorphism τ of Sp₄(R) given in coordinates by the 2×2 minors on the four form-free index pairs (the exterior-square construction Λ²R⁴ ⊃ ker φ ⧸ ⟨ω⟩, which exists only in characteristic 2) exchanges the two root lengths, τ(x_{e₀−e₁}(t)) = x_{2e₁}(t²) and τ(x_{2e₁}(t)) = x_{e₀−e₁}(t), and squares to the Frobenius, τ² = Frob₂; it is transported to the rank-two type-C Chevalley carrier in TauCeti#5920, and the fixed points of its odd powers, which cut out the Suzuki groups ²B₂(2^(2m+1)), are the next step (Carter, *Simple Groups of Lie Type*, §12.3, §13.4; Steinberg, *Endomorphisms of Linear Algebraic Groups*, §11).

name: The intrinsic invariants of an Artin–Wedderburn presentation
text: for a semisimple ring R, any presentation R ≃ ∏ᵢ Matₙᵢ(Dᵢ) has, after one permutation of its blocks, its blocks in bijection with the isomorphism classes of simple R-modules Sᵢ, with nᵢ the multiplicity of Sᵢ in the regular module (the length of its isotypic component) and Dᵢ ≃ (End_R Sᵢ)ᵒᵖ; the uniqueness clause of TauCeti#2718 compared two presentations, and this says what the surviving data are (Lam, *A First Course in Noncommutative Rings*, Ch. 1).

name: The Bruhat order on a Coxeter group
text: for an arbitrary Coxeter system, u ≤ w when w is reached from u by successively multiplying by reflections that increase the length; this is a partial order with the identity as least element, invariant under inversion, and if u ≤ w then u is spelled by a subword of every word for w, reduced or not — the necessary half of the subword property, from the strong exchange condition of TauCeti#5472; the converse, that a subword of a reduced word spells an element below w, is the next step (Björner–Brenti, *Combinatorics of Coxeter Groups*, §2.1–2.2; Humphreys, *Reflection Groups and Coxeter Groups*, §5.9).

name: Student's t as a Gaussian–chi-squared ratio
text: for independent Z ~ N(0, 1) and V ~ χ²_ν, the variable Z / √(V/ν) has Student's t law with ν degrees of freedom, at the level of measures (the pushforward of N(0, 1) ⊗ χ²_ν under (z, v) ↦ z/√(v/ν) is t_ν), by identifying the squared law with Fisher's F(1, ν) and using reflection symmetry; the density of TauCeti#5354 defined the law, and this is its classical construction (Johnson–Kotz–Balakrishnan, *Continuous Univariate Distributions*, vol. 2, ch. 28).

name: The index formula
text: for an integral primitive element θ of a number field K (θ ∈ 𝓞_K with K = ℚ(θ)), disc(minpoly_ℤ θ) = [𝓞_K : ℤ[θ]]² · disc K; hence a prime modulo which the minimal polynomial is squarefree does not divide the index, and a prime divides the index exactly when it divides the conductor exponent of ℤ[θ], which is the hypothesis of Kummer–Dedekind in checkable form (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, I (2.12)).

name: The decomposition group and decomposition field of a place
text: in a finite Galois extension F′/F of function fields, the stabiliser G_Z of a place P has order e(P | F) · f(P | F), P is the only place of F′ above its restriction to the fixed field Z of G_Z, and e = f = 1 below Z, so all of the ramification and of the residue extension of P over F happen above the decomposition field; the surjection of G_Z onto the residue automorphisms with kernel the inertia group is the next step (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Def. 3.8.1, Thm 3.8.2).

name: Skew-zigzag algebras on trees are ordinary
text: over any commutative ring, every skew-zigzag parameter on a forest is gauge equivalent to the constant parameter, so on a finite nontrivial tree every skew-zigzag algebra is isomorphic to the ordinary zigzag algebra; that gauge-equivalent parameters present isomorphic algebras is TauCeti#5891 (Couture, *Skew-Zigzag Algebras*, Thm 4.8, Cor. 4.13).

name: The ray class group of a modulus
text: for a modulus 𝔪 of a number field K, a nonzero integral ideal together with a finite set of real places, the quotient of the fractional ideals prime to 𝔪 by the principal ideals (x) with x ≡ 1 mod× 𝔪 (the prescribed congruence at each prime of the finite part, positivity at the listed real places); an ideal has trivial ray class exactly when it is generated by such an x, the transition maps between moduli compose, and the trivial modulus recovers the class group; finiteness and the ray-class exact sequence are the next milestones (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, VI §1).

name: The Artin map on ideals
text: for a finite abelian extension L/K of number fields and a finite set S of primes outside which L/K is unramified, the homomorphism from the fractional ideals of K supported away from S to Gal(L/K) that sends each prime 𝔭 ∉ S to its Frobenius, the Artin symbol of TauCeti#5346, and is extended multiplicatively; it is determined by those values and is compatible with enlarging S and with restriction to intermediate fields; its kernel, and reciprocity, are the next milestones (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, VI §7).

name: The metric space of graphons
text: graphons on a fixed probability space modulo cut distance zero, in particular modulo measure-preserving rearrangement, made a genuine metric space by the cut metric δ_□, on which every homomorphism density t(F, ·) descends and is Lipschitz with constant the number of edges of F, hence continuous; density of step graphons and compactness are the next steps (Lovász, *Large Networks and Graph Limits*, §8.2; Janson, *Graphons, cut norm and distance, couplings and rearrangements*, §6).

name: The genus field of a quadratic field has Galois group Cl⁺(K)/Cl⁺(K)²
text: for K = ℚ(√d), d squarefree, and K_gen the compositum of the quadratic fields of the prime discriminants dividing disc K, Gal(K_gen/K) ≅ Cl⁺(K)/Cl⁺(K)², and ≅ Cl(K)/Cl(K)² for d < 0, via the principal genus theorem: a narrow ideal class is a square exactly when every genus character is trivial on it; the summit of the 2-rank formula of TauCeti#5899, with the identification of the isomorphism with the inverse Artin map not yet proved (Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, Thm 3.15, §6.A).

name: The fundamental group is the automorphism group of the fibre functor
text: for X path-connected, locally path-connected and semilocally simply connected, π₁(X, x₀) is the automorphism group of the functor sending a covering space of X, finite or not, to its fibre over x₀, a loop class acting by monodromy; the input is a reconstruction of a monoid from its G-sets as the endomorphisms of the forgetful functor (Lenstra, *Galois theory for schemes*, §3; Szamuely, *Galois Groups and Fundamental Groups*, Ch. 2).

name: A universal cover exists exactly when the base is semilocally simply connected
text: a path-connected, locally path-connected space admits a simply connected covering space if and only if it is semilocally simply connected; the construction was in place, adapted from Kim Morrison's open mathlib4#38292, and the new half is necessity, via a local section of any local homeomorphism whose source has only null-homotopic loops (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, after Prop. 1.36).

name: Frobenius–Schur indicator −1 means a quaternionic structure
text: an irreducible unitary representation of a compact group on a finite-dimensional complex space has ν₂ = −1 exactly when it carries a conjugate-linear J commuting with the action with J² = −1, completing the structure-map reading of the trichotomy of TauCeti#4313, where ν₂ = 1 is a real structure, equivalently realizability over ℝ (Bröcker–tom Dieck, *Representations of Compact Lie Groups*, II §6).

name: The Alexander polynomial of a braid closure from the Burau representation
text: the determinant of Burau(b) − 1 with its last row and column deleted is unchanged by conjugation and multiplied by a unit under the two Markov stabilizations, so Markov-equivalent braids have the same value up to a unit of ℤ[T, T⁻¹]; on σ₀³, the trefoil braid, it is associated to the T − 1 + T⁻¹ of the Seifert-matrix route of TauCeti#3948, and at t = −1 it separates the trefoil braid from the trivial one; Markov's theorem itself is not formalized (Birman, *Braids, Links, and Mapping Class Groups*, Thm 3.11).

name: Tate cohomology of a finite cyclic group is two-periodic
text: for G finite cyclic with generator g and any representation M over a commutative ring, every even Tate degree is the homology of M →N→ M →ρ(g)−1→ M and every odd degree that of the same maps in the other order, in all of ℤ including Ĥ⁰ and Ĥ⁻¹, so Ĥ^m(G, M) ≅ Ĥ^n(G, M) whenever m ≡ n mod 2; read off Mathlib's Tate groups, and the periodicity behind the Herbrand quotient of TauCeti#5764 (Serre, *Local Fields*, VIII §4).

name: The Pontryagin dual of the circle is ℤ
text: every continuous character of ℝ/Tℤ is a Fourier monomial x ↦ e^(2πinx/T) for a unique integer n, with modulus one falling out rather than assumed, so n ↦ fourier n is an isomorphism ℤ ≅ PontryaginDual(ℝ/Tℤ); the exhaustion half of the circle's Peter–Weyl worked example (Rudin, *Fourier Analysis on Groups*, Ch. 1).

name: Mollification converges in Lᵖ
text: for 1 ≤ p < ∞, an additive Haar measure on a finite-dimensional real normed space and Banach-space-valued f ∈ Lᵖ, averaging against a normalized smooth bump, as a Bochner integral in Lᵖ itself, is a contraction of Lᵖ and converges strongly to f as the radii of the bumps tend to zero; the Lᵖ input for Meyers–Serrin (Brezis, *Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and PDE*, Prop. 4.21).

name: The ratio of two independent standard Gaussians is Cauchy
text: for independent X, Y ~ N(0, 1), X/Y has the standard Cauchy law, at the level of measures the pushforward of N(0, 1) ⊗ N(0, 1) under (x, y) ↦ x/y, through Student's t with one degree of freedom from TauCeti#5935 (Johnson–Kotz–Balakrishnan, *Continuous Univariate Distributions*, vol. 1).

name: The symplectic group is reductive
text: over every field, in every rank and every characteristic, Sp₂ₘ is smooth and geometrically connected with no nontrivial connected normal smooth unipotent closed subgroup over an algebraic closure, because its standard representation is faithful and simple; the symplectic companion of GLₙ in TauCeti#4394 (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, §§19.b, 24.6).

name: The ideal class group of an affine model of a function field is finite
text: for a function field F/k with k finite and R any Dedekind k-subalgebra of F with fraction field F, ClassGroup R is finite, with no separability hypothesis and no chosen rational subfield, since R has a place at infinity whose class dies in ClassGroup R and Cl⁰(F) is finite; with a rational place at infinity the class number of R divides h_F; Mathlib has the integral closure of 𝔽_q[X] under separability, by a Minkowski-style route (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Prop. 5.1.3).

name: Joint dissociation is corner-tail triviality
text: a jointly exchangeable array X_{ij} is dissociated, blocks over disjoint index sets being independent, exactly when the corner tail ⋂ₙ σ(X_{ij} : i, j ≥ n) is trivial; the zero-one law was known and the converse is new and representation-free, separating the ergodic form of the Aldous–Hoover representation from the general one (Kallenberg, *Probabilistic Symmetries and Invariance Principles*, Ch. 7).

name: The character table of Sₙ and its orthogonality relations
text: the integer table χ^μ(ν) of Specht character values on cycle types is the complex character table of Sₙ, rows reindexed by the classification of TauCeti#5649, so over ℤ the columns satisfy Σ_μ χ^μ(ν)χ^μ(ν′) = z_ν δ_{νν′}, the rows Σ_ν χ^μ(ν)χ^{μ′}(ν)/z_ν = δ_{μμ′}, and Σ_{μ ⊢ n} (dim S^μ)² = n!; the Murnaghan–Nakayama rule is the next step (James, *The Representation Theory of the Symmetric Groups*, Ch. 6).

name: The Riemann–Roch theorem
text: for an algebraic function field F/k with exact constant field k there is a divisor W with ℓ(D) = deg D + 1 − g + ℓ(W − D) for every divisor D, namely the divisor (ω) of any nonzero Weil differential, with the duality L(W − D) ≃ Ω_F(D), x ↦ xω, giving ℓ(W − D) = i(D); so the canonical class is well defined, of degree 2g − 2 with ℓ(W) = g, and a divisor is canonical exactly when deg D = 2g − 2 and ℓ(D) ≥ g; the summit above Riemann's theorem of TauCeti#4463 (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Thm 1.5.15, Prop. 1.6.2).

name: Perron's formula
text: for a Dirichlet series L(s) = Σ f(n) n^(−s) converging absolutely on Re s = c > 0 and an integer N ≥ 1, (2πi)⁻¹ ∫_(c−iT)^(c+iT) L(s) N^s s⁻¹ ds → Σ_(n<N) f(n) + f(N)/2 as T → ∞, the endpoint entering with half weight, and for non-integer x the truncated integral differs from Σ_(n<x) f(n) by at most Σ |f(n)| (x/n)^c / (πT |log(x/n)|), the truncated Perron formula with its explicit error term (Davenport, *Multiplicative Number Theory*, Ch. 17).

name: The profinite completion of π₁ is the automorphism group of the finite-cover fibre functor
text: for X path-connected, locally path-connected and semilocally simply connected, π̂₁(X, x₀) is isomorphic as a topological group to the automorphism group of the fibre functor on finite covering spaces of X, acting on each fibre by the unique continuous extension of monodromy; the finite-cover counterpart of TauCeti#6023, via Mathlib's Galois-category recognition theorem and the fact that the profinite completion of any group is the fundamental group of its finite G-sets (Szamuely, *Galois Groups and Fundamental Groups*, Ch. 2).

name: Spin₃ ≅ SL₂
text: over a field K with 2 ≠ 0, the Spin group of a split three-dimensional quadratic space, a hyperbolic plane plus a line, is isomorphic to SL₂(K), the even Clifford algebra being M₂(K) with Clifford reversal as the adjugate, and under this isomorphism the spin representation is the standard two-dimensional representation of SL₂; over a separably closed field every nondegenerate ternary form qualifies (Fulton–Harris, *Representation Theory*, Lecture 20).

name: The ray class group of a modulus is finite
text: for every modulus 𝔪 of a number field K, an integral ideal 𝔪₀ together with a set of real places, Cl_𝔪(K) is finite, and the units congruent to 1 mod× 𝔪 have finite index in 𝓞_Kˣ; the proof follows the ray class exact sequence, the map to Cl(K) having finite image and kernel the principal ideals prime to 𝔪, in which the ray has finite index by reduction to (𝓞_K/𝔪₀)ˣ; the group was TauCeti#5842 (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, VI §1).

name: The inertia group of a place
text: in a finite Galois extension F′/F of function fields, the decomposition group G_Z(P) of a place P of F′ acts on the residue field F′_P over that of P ∩ F, the action is onto and its kernel is the inertia group G_T(P), so G_Z/G_T ≅ Aut(F′_P / F_(P∩F)), of order the separable residue degree, and |G_T| = e(P | P ∩ F) when the residue extension is separable; the second half of the theorem whose first half, |G_Z| = e·f and the decomposition field, was TauCeti#5871 (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Thm 3.8.2).

name: Morse functions are generic
text: for a C² function f on an open subset U of a finite-dimensional real normed space and almost every linear functional a, for Haar measure on the dual, every critical point of f − a in U is nondegenerate, because f − a has a degenerate critical point exactly when a is a critical value of df, a map between spaces of the same dimension to which the equal-dimensional Sard theorem applies; so Morse perturbations are dense and can be taken arbitrarily small (Guillemin–Pollack, *Differential Topology*, Ch. 1 §7).

name: The formal group of an elliptic curve is E₁(K_v)
text: for a Weierstrass curve over the valuation ring 𝒪_v of the completion K_v of the fraction field of a Dedekind domain at a height-one prime, the parametrisation t ↦ (t/w(t), −1/w(t)) is an injective homomorphism from the formal group Ê(𝔪_v) on the maximal ideal to E(K_v) whose image is the point at infinity together with the points whose x-coordinate has a pole, so Ê(𝔪_v) ≅ E₁(K_v); the image is described through the valuation of x since no reduction map on points exists yet (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, VII.2.2).

name: Weil divisors are Cartier divisors on a curve
text: on a Noetherian integral scheme all of whose points have codimension at most one and whose codimension-one local rings are discrete valuation rings, every Weil divisor is locally principal, and taking the orders of local equations at codimension-one points is an isomorphism of groups from Cartier divisors to Weil divisors, inverse to gluing the local equations of a Weil divisor (Hartshorne, *Algebraic Geometry*, II.6.11; Stacks Project, Tag 0BE9).

name: Hopf's boundary-point lemma
text: a function continuous on a closed ball of a finite-dimensional real inner product space, C² with Δu ≥ 0 inside, and differentiable at a boundary point where it attains a strict maximum over the closed ball has strictly positive outward derivative there; proved in every dimension by the classical radial barrier (Evans, *PDE*, §6.4.2; Gilbarg–Trudinger, Lemma 3.4).

name: The Cholesky decomposition
text: every positive-definite real symmetric matrix A factors as A = L Lᵀ with L lower triangular and positive on the diagonal, built from Mathlib's LDL decomposition; uniqueness of L is the next step (Horn–Johnson, *Matrix Analysis*, §7.2).

name: The Diaconis–Freedman representation
text: a Markov exchangeable process on a countable state space (law invariant under permutations of finite paths preserving initial state and transition counts) that is recurrent and almost surely visits every state is a mixture of Markov chains, because its successor array is row exchangeable; the case of a process missing a state stays open (Diaconis–Freedman, "de Finetti's theorem for Markov chains", Ann. Probab. 8 (1980)).

name: Every multiquadratic field lies in a cyclotomic field
text: for nonzero rationals d₁, …, dₙ, ℚ(√d₁, …, √dₙ) ⊆ ℚ(ζ_N) with N = 4∏ᵢ|num dᵢ · den dᵢ|, hence every finite Galois extension of ℚ of exponent dividing 2 embeds in a cyclotomic field; the engine is the quadratic Gauss sum, which places √p* in ℚ(ζ_p) for p* = (−1)^((p−1)/2) p — the multiquadratic case of the Kronecker–Weber theorem, the general theorem untouched (Ireland–Rosen, Ch. 6).

name: Sylow pro-p subgroups of a profinite group are conjugate
text: any two Sylow pro-p subgroups (closed pro-p subgroups of index prime to p in every finite quotient) are conjugate, so a normal one is unique; with Lagrange's theorem for profinite groups, |G| = |H|·[G : H] as supernatural numbers for closed H (TauCeti#6128), and multiplicativity of the index in a tower (TauCeti#6230); existence of Sylow pro-p subgroups is a separate open PR (Ribes–Zalesskii, *Profinite Groups*, §2.3).

name: The Stasheff identities are the square-zero condition on the bar construction
text: the degree-one coderivation b of the reduced tensor coalgebra built from suspended operations mₙ satisfies b ∘ b = 0 exactly when all the Stasheff identities Σ ± m_{r+1+t}(1^r ⊗ m_s ⊗ 1^t) = 0 hold, arity 1–4 written out with the Getzler–Jones/Keller signs; A∞-algebras are the next definition (Keller, *Introduction to A-infinity algebras*, §3.6).

name: The 2-rank of the class group of a quadratic field is t − 1 or t − 2
text: for K quadratic with t ramified rational primes, the ordinary class group Cl(K) has 2-rank t − 1 or t − 2, both occurring (ℚ(√10), ℚ(√3)): the narrow formula 2-rank Cl⁺(K) = t − 1 of TauCeti#5899 drops by at most one because the kernel of Cl⁺(K) → Cl(K) has at most two elements; and the isomorphism Gal(K_gen/K) ≅ Cl⁺(K)/Cl⁺(K)² of TauCeti#6073 is now identified with the inverse of the Artin map on ideals prime to 2·disc K (Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, §6.A).

name: Complete Bernstein functions, and Bernstein functions through their exponentials
text: complete Bernstein functions g(t) = a + bt + ∫₀^∞ t/(t + x) dμ(x) are Bernstein, and f is a Stieltjes function iff t ↦ t f(t) extends to a complete Bernstein function (Schilling–Song–Vondraček, *Bernstein Functions*, Thms 6.2, 7.3; Pick-function form not formalised); and f is a Bernstein function iff f ≥ 0 and every e^(−xf), x > 0, is completely monotone on (0, ∞) and continuous at 0, the Laplace-exponent characterisation (Thm 3.7).

name: The differential criterion for separability of an isogeny
text: an isogeny φ : E₁ → E₂ of elliptic curves is separable iff φ*ω₂ ≠ 0, ω the invariant differential (Silverman II.4.2(c)); the pullback of ω is additive, (f + g)*ω = f*ω + g*ω (III.5.2), now that Hom(E₁, E₂) is an abelian group (TauCeti#6302), so over a finite field 1 − π is separable since Frobenius kills ω (III.5.5), the step by which #E(𝔽_q) becomes deg(1 − π) on the way to the Hasse bound, not yet proved.

name: The reflection length of a permutation
text: the least number of transpositions whose product is a permutation σ of an n-element set is n minus the number of orbits of σ, fixed points counted, as multiplying by a transposition merges two orbits or splits one (Dénes, 1959).

name: Higher ramification groups of a place
text: for a place P of a function-field extension F'/F, G_i(P) = {σ ∈ G_Z(P) : ord_P(σz − z) ≥ i + 1 for all z ∈ 𝒪_P} in lower numbering: G₀ is the inertia group, the G_i decrease, are normal in G_Z and meet in 1, G_{i+1}/G_{i+2} is elementary abelian in characteristic p, and G₁ = 1 in characteristic zero; Mathlib stops at the inertia group; G₀/G₁ cyclic of order prime to p and Hilbert's different formula are the next rungs (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, 3.8.4–3.8.5).

name: Fans of toric cones
text: a finite family of toric cones closed under faces with pairwise intersections a face of each, with support, completeness, subfans, the fan of a single cone, and morphisms of fans determined by their lattice map; the zero cone lies in every nonempty fan, and gluing a toric variety from a fan is a later target (Fulton, *Introduction to Toric Varieties*, §1.4).

name: Newforms
text: Miyake's primitive form: a cusp form of level Γ₁(N), weight k and nebentypus χ, eigen for the Γ₀(N) Hecke ring at every index coprime to N, in the new subspace and normalised by a₁ = 1; multiplicity one and the eigenvalues at bad indices are the Atkin–Lehner theorems still to come (Miyake, *Modular Forms*, §4.6).

name: Hölder spaces
text: the bounded continuous globally α-Hölder functions X → E with norm ‖f‖_∞ + [f]_α form a Banach space when E is; the zeroth member of the C^{k,α} scale for the Schauder estimates (Gilbarg–Trudinger, §4.1).

name: Atkin–Lehner operators W_Q
text: for an exact divisor Q ∥ N, the integral matrices [Qa, b; Nc, Qd] of determinant Q normalize Γ₀(N) and any two differ by an element of Γ₀(N), so slashing by one is a well-defined operator W_Q on M_k(Γ₀(N)) and S_k(Γ₀(N)), with W₁ = 1, W_N the Fricke operator and W_Q² = Q^{k−2} in un-normalized form; the normalized involution and the newform eigenvalues ±1 are still to come (Atkin–Lehner, *Math. Ann.* 185 (1970); Diamond–Shurman §5).

name: The Sylow theorems for profinite groups
text: every profinite group has a Sylow pro-p subgroup, a closed pro-p subgroup whose image in each finite quotient is a Sylow p-subgroup, built as the inverse limit of the finite Sylow subgroups; every pro-p subgroup lies in a conjugate of any given Sylow pro-p subgroup, and the Sylow pro-p subgroups are exactly the maximal pro-p subgroups; with the conjugacy of TauCeti#6278 this completes the Sylow theory of profinite groups (Ribes–Zalesskii, *Profinite Groups*, §2.3).

name: SOₙ is connected and reductive
text: over every field of characteristic ≠ 2 and for every n, the special orthogonal group scheme of the standard symmetric form is geometrically connected and reductive, connectedness coming from Cartan–Dieudonné, which writes a rotation as a product of pairs of reflections, each pair joined to the identity along an explicit Laurent-polynomial path; SOₙ joins GLₙ, SLₙ, Sp₂ₙ and the tori among the library's reductive groups (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, §§18.c, 21).

name: Joint dissociation is ergodicity of diagonal relabelling
text: a jointly exchangeable array is jointly dissociated, its blocks on disjoint index sets independent, exactly when the diagonal action of the finitary permutations of ℕ, relabelling both coordinates at once, is ergodic for its law; this closes the triangle dissociation ↔ corner-tail triviality (TauCeti#5841) ↔ ergodicity, and is not the Aldous–Hoover representation itself (Kallenberg, *Probabilistic Symmetries and Invariance Principles*, Ch. 7).

name: Spin(n) is path-connected
text: for n ≥ 2 the compact real Spin group is path-connected, since −1 and every product of two unit-vector reflections lie in the identity component; and over any field with 2 invertible Spin(Q) is a double cover of the kernel of the spinor norm, packaged as the extension 1 → ℤ/2 → Spin(Q) → ker θ → 1 inside SO(Q); simple connectivity of Spin(n) for n ≥ 3 is the next step (Lawson–Michelsohn, *Spin Geometry*, I §2).

name: Test functions are dense in W^{1,p}(ℝⁿ)
text: for 1 ≤ p < ∞, W^{1,p}_0(ℝⁿ) = W^{1,p}(ℝⁿ): every whole-space Sobolev function is a Sobolev-norm limit of smooth compactly supported functions, by mollification and cut-off; Mathlib has the density in Lᵖ, and the Meyers–Serrin theorem on a domain is the next milestone (Evans, *PDE*, §5.3.1; Brezis, §9.1).

name: Homotopy groups are homotopy invariants
text: a homotopy equivalence e : X ≃ Y induces isomorphisms πₙ(X, x) ≅ πₙ(Y, e(x)) in every dimension, via the trace formula that freely homotopic maps induce the same map up to base-point change along the trace of the homotopy; hence asphericity and the K(G, 1) property are homotopy invariants. Mathlib has the fundamental-groupoid case; the higher πₙ are new (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, §4.1).

name: Every positive root is a Weyl reflection of a simple root
text: for a finite quiver with positive definite Tits form q, the nonnegative integer vectors with q(d) = 1 are exactly the images of the standard basis vectors under finite sequences of simple reflections; the root-lattice input to the reflection-functor proof of Gabriel's theorem, which is not itself claimed (Bernstein–Gelfand–Ponomarev; Assem–Simson–Skowroński, VII.5).

name: h⁺ = h for a real quadratic field iff a unit has norm −1
text: for K = ℚ(√d), d > 0, the narrow class number equals the class number exactly when 𝓞_K has a unit of norm −1, that is, when the negative Pell equation is solvable, and for every quadratic field h⁺ ≤ 2h; with the narrow 2-rank formula of TauCeti#5899 this decides when the ordinary class group has 2-rank t − 1 (Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, §6.A).

name: Uniqueness of almost-split sequences
text: in a preadditive balanced category, two almost-split sequences whose left ends have local endomorphism rings and whose right ends are isomorphic are isomorphic as short complexes, and any morphism between them that is invertible at the right end is invertible; the uniqueness half of the Auslander–Reiten theorem, existence still open (Auslander–Reiten–Smalø, Ch. V; Assem–Simson–Skowroński, IV.1).

name: Strong multiplicity one for newforms
text: two newforms of level N, weight k and the same nebentypus whose Hecke eigenvalues (equivalently, q-expansion coefficients) agree at every index coprime to N outside a finite set are equal, nothing being assumed at the primes dividing the level; the engine is the Atkin–Lehner Main Lemma at fixed nebentypus, that a cusp form in S_k(Γ₁(N), χ) whose q-expansion vanishes at every index coprime to N is old, indeed Σ_{p∣N} V_p f_p with f_p of level N/p; the Main Lemma without a fixed character is not claimed (Miyake, *Modular Forms*, Thm 4.6.12 and Lemma 4.6.8; Diamond–Shurman §5.7 and Thm 5.8.2).

name: Witt's cancellation theorem
text: over a field of characteristic ≠ 2, if q ⊥ q₁ ≅ q ⊥ q₂ with q regular and finite-dimensional then q₁ ≅ q₂, proved through hyperplane reflections; so the isometry classes of regular forms are cancellative under ⊥, the input the Witt ring needs (Lam, *Introduction to Quadratic Forms over Fields*, I.4.2).

name: Every central simple algebra has a finite separable splitting field
text: a finite-dimensional central simple algebra over K becomes a matrix algebra over a finite subextension of the separable closure, by descending a matrix presentation over K^sep to the field its matrix units generate; with the separably closed case of TauCeti#4501 this closes the splitting-field milestone (Gille–Szamuely, *Central Simple Algebras and Galois Cohomology*, §2.2).

name: The action of π₁ on the higher homotopy groups
text: π₁(X, x) acts on πₙ(X, x) by group automorphisms for n ≥ 1 (the π₁-module structure on πₙ for n ≥ 2, conjugation for n = 1), and two classes lie in the same orbit exactly when they are freely homotopic, so the orbit set is the set of free homotopy classes of maps Sⁿ → X into the component of x and the action is trivial on a simply connected space (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, §4.1).

name: Schur–Weyl duality for the image of k[GLₙ]
text: over an infinite field in which d! ≠ 0, the images of the group algebras k[GLₙ] and k[S_d] in End((kⁿ)^{⊗d}) are each other's centralizers; the duality announced with TauCeti#5127 had the span of all diagonal operators f^{⊗d} in place of the image of k[GLₙ], now identified by the Zariski density of GLₙ, completing the classical statement (Fulton–Harris, Lecture 6; Procesi, *Lie Groups*, Ch. 9).

name: Dedekind's discriminant theorem, relative form
text: for a finite separable extension of Dedekind domains A ⊆ B, with the relative discriminant ideal 𝔡_{B/A} defined as the norm of the different, a nonzero prime of A divides 𝔡_{B/A} exactly when some prime above it ramifies, for number fields exactly when a prime above it has ramification index > 1, together with the tower formula and 𝔡_{𝓞_K/ℤ} = (disc K); Mathlib has the criterion for the absolute discriminant over ℤ, this is the relative one (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, III.2.10 and III.2.12).

name: The 2-rank of the class group of a real quadratic field
text: for K = ℚ(√d), d > 0, with t ramified primes, the 2-rank of Cl(K) is t − 1 exactly when every prime discriminant dividing disc K is positive, that is, when no prime ≡ 3 (mod 4) divides d, and is t − 2 otherwise, by evaluating the genus characters on the narrow class of (√d), χ_P([√d]⁺) = sign P; this settles the t − 1 or t − 2 dichotomy of TauCeti#6270, extending the norm −1 criterion of TauCeti#6275 (Lemmermeyer, *Reciprocity Laws*, §2.2; Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, §6.A).

name: Fuchsian groups act properly discontinuously
text: every discrete subgroup of PSL(2, ℝ) acts properly discontinuously on the upper half-plane, descended from Mathlib's proper SL(2, ℝ) action; and in general the free locus of a properly discontinuous action on a locally compact Hausdorff space is open and its orbit projection is a covering map (Katok, *Fuchsian Groups*, Ch. 2).

name: deg(1 − π_q) = #E(𝔽_q)

reference.text: Voyager, TauCeti#6446, TauCeti#6466, TauCeti#6455, TauCeti#6464, TauCeti#6463

text: for an elliptic curve over 𝔽_q the isogeny 1 − π_q, with π_q the q-power Frobenius, has degree the number of rational points, the first input of the Hasse bound; alongside it, multiplication by n has kernel the rational n-torsion, equals n·id in End(E), is separable exactly when n ≠ 0 in the base field, and the degree satisfies deg(n·φ) = n²·deg φ; the order #E[n] = n² is the next step (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, III.4–III.6, V.1.1).

name: The normalized Atkin–Lehner involutions 𝒲_Q
text: the normalization promised with yesterday's W_Q: 𝒲_Q = (√Q)^{2−k}·W_Q is an involution of M_k(Γ₀(N)) and of S_k(Γ₀(N)) at every weight, and 𝒲_Q ∘ 𝒲_R = 𝒲_{QR/gcd(Q,R)²}, so the exact divisors of N, a Boolean group ≅ (ℤ/2)^{ω(N)}, act through commuting involutions; the eigenvalues ε_Q on newforms wait on the newform theory (Atkin–Lehner, *Math. Ann.* 185 (1970)).

name: A∞-algebras
text: nonunital, uncurved A∞-algebras on a ℤ-graded module: operations m_n of degree 2 − n packaged as a square-zero degree-one coderivation of the reduced tensor coalgebra, with the equivalence to the unsuspended Stasheff identities and a constructor from them (Keller, *Introduction to A-infinity algebras and modules*, §3).

name: Witt decomposition
text: over a field of characteristic ≠ 2, every regular quadratic form on a finite-dimensional space is isometric to m hyperbolic planes ⊥ an anisotropic form, and m and the anisotropic summand are determined by the isometry class, defining the Witt index and the anisotropic part, with rank q = 2·(Witt index) + rank(anisotropic part); the degenerate case and the maximal-totally-isotropic description of the index are still to come (Lam, *Introduction to Quadratic Forms over Fields*, I.4.1).

name: The Weierstrass gap theorem
text: at a rational place P of a function field of genus g > 0 with integrally closed constants, exactly g positive integers are gaps, that is, are the pole order at P of no function regular elsewhere; 1 is a gap and every gap is at most 2g − 1, by counting the jumps of ℓ(nP) (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Thm 1.6.8).

name: McDiarmid's bounded-differences inequality
text: if a measurable function f of finitely many i.i.d. coordinates changes by at most cᵢ when only the i-th coordinate changes, then f − 𝔼f is sub-Gaussian with variance proxy Σ cᵢ²/4, whence ℙ(f − 𝔼f ≥ t) ≤ exp(−2t²/Σ cᵢ²) through Mathlib's sub-Gaussian API; the concentration engine for the sampling convergence of graphons (McDiarmid, *On the method of bounded differences*, 1989).

name: The Mackey decomposition as an isomorphism of representations
text: for subgroups H, K of an arbitrary group G and a representation A of H over any commutative ring, Res_K Ind_H^G A ≅ ⨁_{KsH ∈ K\G/H} Ind_{K ∩ sHs⁻¹}^K Res(ˢA), naturally in A; the character form of TauCeti#2087 needed a finite group and gave an equality of characters, this is the isomorphism itself with no finiteness assumed (Serre, *Linear Representations of Finite Groups*, §7.3).

name: E[n] has n² points, and E(F) ≅ Cl⁰(F(E))
text: over an algebraically closed field in which n is invertible, the kernel of multiplication by n on a Weierstrass curve has exactly n² points, the step flagged yesterday, from [n] having separable degree n² and the converse that a nonsingular point where the division polynomial ψₙ vanishes is killed by n; and for an affine Weierstrass curve with Dedekind coordinate ring the point group is the degree-zero divisor class group of the function field, P ↦ [(P) − (O)], the input the divisor construction of the Weil pairing consumes (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, III.3.4, III.6.4).

name: Cartan–Dieudonné with the sharp bound, and Spin(n) is compact
text: over any field of characteristic ≠ 2, every isometry of an n-dimensional nondegenerate quadratic space is a product of at most n reflections, a determinant-one isometry of an even number of them; the generation form of TauCeti#2492 carried no bound, and Mathlib has the bound for real inner-product spaces only; hence Spin(n) is compact, a continuous image of a fixed finite product of unit spheres (Lawson–Michelsohn, *Spin Geometry*, I §2).

name: The loop-space shift πₙ₊₁(ΩX) ≅ πₙ₊₂(X)
text: homotopy rel boundary of generalized loops is path-connectedness in the compact-open loop space, so πₙ(X, x) is the set of path components of ΩⁿX and the cubical currying Ω^M(Ω^N X) ≃ Ω^{M⊔N} X descends to group isomorphisms π_M(Ω^N X) ≅ π_{M⊔N}(X), in particular πₘ₊₁(ΩX) ≅ πₘ₊₂(X) and π₀(ΩX) ≅ π₁(X); Mathlib has the homeomorphism of loop spaces but not its effect on homotopy groups (Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, §4.1).

name: Galois descent produces a torus
text: for a finite Galois extension L/k and a lattice M with any action of Gal(L/k), the invariants of L[M] under the simultaneous action on coefficients and exponents are the coordinate ring of a torus over k split by L, in any characteristic, and its characters over L recover M with its Galois action; the existence half of the anti-equivalence between tori split by L and Gal(L/k)-lattices, whose inverse is still to come (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, Thm 12.23).

name: Primitivity and 2-transitivity of polynomial Galois groups
text: for an irreducible separable p over F with a root α, the Galois group is 2-transitive on the roots exactly when p/(X − α) stays irreducible over F(α), and since the blocks containing α correspond, order-reversingly, to the intermediate fields of F(α)/F, the action is primitive exactly when F(α)/F has no proper intermediate field, as in prime degree (Wielandt, *Finite Permutation Groups*, Thm 7.5).

name: The Dirichlet distribution
text: Dir(a) on the standard simplex, the law of independent Gamma(aᵢ) variables divided by their sum; the total of any block s of coordinates is Beta(Σ_s aᵢ, Σ_{sᶜ} aᵢ), merging coordinates along a surjection gives the Dirichlet law with summed parameters, and the mean aᵢ/a₀ and covariance −aᵢaⱼ/(a₀²(a₀ + 1)) are computed; the density on the simplex is next (Johnson–Kotz–Balakrishnan, *Continuous Multivariate Distributions*, ch. 49).

name: The multivariate Gamma function
text: Γ_p(a) = π^{p(p−1)/4} ∏_{i<p} Γ(a − i/2), with Γ_{p+q}(a) = π^{pq/2} Γ_p(a) Γ_q(a − p/2), Γ₁ = Γ, positivity for a > (p − 1)/2 and the exact vanishing locus outside it; the cone integral ∫_{A>0} det(A)^{a−(p+1)/2} e^{−tr A} dA = Γ_p(a) that makes it the Wishart normalizing constant is proved in dimension 0 only so far (Muirhead, *Aspects of Multivariate Statistical Theory*, §2.1).

name: The strong maximum principle for subharmonic functions
text: on an open preconnected set U in a finite-dimensional real inner product space, a C² function with Δu ≥ 0 that attains its maximum over U at a point of U is constant on U, proved through Hopf's boundary-point lemma (Gilbarg–Trudinger, Thm 3.5), together with the strong minimum and comparison principles and their versions for functions continuous up to the boundary; this extends the planar harmonic case of TauCeti#1724 to subharmonic functions in every dimension.

name: Witt's extension theorem
text: over a field of characteristic ≠ 2, an isometry between two subspaces of a finite-dimensional quadratic space on which the form is nondegenerate extends to an isometry of the whole space, with no nondegeneracy assumed of the ambient form (Lam, *Introduction to Quadratic Forms over Fields*, I.4.9); it joins the cancellation and decomposition theorems of TauCeti#6439 and TauCeti#6544.

name: The ray class number formula
text: for a modulus 𝔪 of a number field K, h_𝔪 · [𝓞_Kˣ : U_𝔪] = h · #(𝓞_K/𝔪₀)ˣ · 2^#𝔪_∞, read off the now complete ray class exact sequence 1 → U_𝔪 → 𝓞_Kˣ → (𝓞_K/𝔪₀)ˣ × {±1}^𝔪_∞ → Cl_𝔪 → Cl → 1, with the narrow case h⁺ · [𝓞_Kˣ : 𝓞_K^{ˣ,+}] = h · 2^{r₁} (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, VI (1.10)–(1.11)).

name: The signature of a knot is an S-equivalence invariant
text: the signature of V + Vᵀ for a Seifert matrix V is unchanged by unimodular congruence and by the two enlargements that record adding a tube to the Seifert surface, so it is an invariant of the knot and not of the chosen surface; the trefoil has signature −2 and the figure-eight 0 (Lickorish, *An Introduction to Knot Theory*, Ch. 8; Murasugi 1965), complementing the Alexander polynomial of TauCeti#3948.

name: Krull dimension is invariant under integral extensions and under base field extension
text: an injective integral extension R → S satisfies dim S = dim R (incomparability plus going up, Atiyah–Macdonald 5.9 and 5.11), and for a finitely generated algebra A over a field k and any field extension K/k, dim(K ⊗_k A) = dim A, through Noether normalisation (Stacks 00OW).

name: The pro-p Frattini subgroup is the closure of Gᵖ[G,G]
text: for a profinite group G and a prime p, the intersection Φ_p(G) of the open normal subgroups of index p is the closure of the subgroup generated by the p-th powers and the commutators; G/Φ_p(G) is elementary abelian, Φ_p(G) is characteristic and is carried onto Φ_p(H) by any continuous surjection G → H, and Φ_p(G) = 1 exactly when G itself is elementary abelian (Ribes–Zalesskii, *Profinite Groups*, §2.8).

name: The Galois group of a compositum is a fibre product
text: for finite Galois subextensions K, L of a field extension of F, a pair (σ, τ) ∈ Gal(K/F) × Gal(L/F) comes from Gal(KL/F) exactly when σ and τ agree on K ∩ L, so Gal(KL/F) ≅ Gal(K/F) ×_{Gal(K∩L/F)} Gal(L/F); for separable polynomials p and q this describes the image of Gal(pq) → Gal(p) × Gal(q), which is onto precisely when the two splitting fields meet in F.

name: Splitting of a prime in the inertia field
text: for L/K a finite Galois extension of fraction fields of Dedekind domains, P a prime above p with inertia field E and 𝔓_E = P ∩ 𝓞_E, and the residue field at p perfect: P is the only prime above 𝔓_E, e(P/𝔓_E) = e(P/p) and f(P/𝔓_E) = 1, while 𝔓_E is unramified over p with the full residue degree f(P/p) (Neukirch I (9.6)); Mathlib has the decomposition-field row of Hilbert's table, and this supplies the inertia-field row.

name: The double coset law for splitting in a non-Galois subfield
text: for M/K finite Galois with group G, a subgroup H with fixed field E, and a prime Q of 𝓞_M above p with decomposition group D, the primes of 𝓞_E above p are in bijection with the double cosets H\G/D via σ ↦ σQ ∩ 𝓞_E (Neukirch I §9, where the proof is left to the reader; Janusz, *Algebraic Number Fields*, Ch. I).

name: The Monge problem
text: the Monge value of a cost c between measures μ and ν is the infimum of ∫ c(x, T x) dμ over measurable maps T pushing μ to ν (and ∞ when there is none); it dominates the Kantorovich value of TauCeti#3875, a transport map attains the Kantorovich value exactly when its graph coupling is an optimal plan, and the inequality is strict for a Dirac source and an atomless target (Villani, *Topics in Optimal Transportation*, Ch. 1).

name: The operator geometric mean
text: a # b = √a · √(√a⁻¹ b √a⁻¹) · √a in an algebra with a continuous functional calculus; for a strictly positive and b ≥ 0 it is the unique nonnegative solution of the Riccati equation x a⁻¹ x = b, it is symmetric in a and b, commutes with inversion, and satisfies the operator arithmetic–geometric mean inequality 2(a # b) ≤ a + b (Pusz–Woronowicz 1975; Ando, *Topics on operator inequalities*); for matrices, A S A = T has exactly one positive semidefinite solution A when S is positive definite and T positive semidefinite.

name: The normed complexification of a real Banach space
text: X_ℂ = X ⊕ iX with the Taylor norm ‖z‖ = sup_{|w|=1} ‖Re(wz)‖, which contains X isometrically, is complete when X is, and gives every bounded real operator T a unique complex-linear extension T_ℂ with ‖T_ℂ‖ = ‖T‖ (Muñoz–Sarantopoulos–Tonge, *Studia Math.* 134 (1999)).

name: The Newtonian kernel is a fundamental solution of −Δ
text: for n ≥ 3 and Gₙ(x) = ‖x‖^(2−n)/(n(n−2)ωₙ), ∫ Δf · Gₙ = −f(0) for every C² function f of compact support on ℝⁿ, i.e. −ΔGₙ = δ₀; on the way, integration in polar coordinates for every integrable function, where Mathlib had radial functions only (Evans, *PDE*, §2.2.1).

name: Witt's chain equivalence theorem, and real forms are classified by signature
text: over a field with 2 invertible, two diagonal forms ⟨a₁, …, aₙ⟩, ⟨b₁, …, bₙ⟩ of rank n ≥ 2 are isometric exactly when a chain of binary changes, each an isometry of two coefficients, connects them (Lam, I.5.2); and over ℝ, two nondegenerate forms are isometric exactly when their signatures agree; Mathlib has both halves of Sylvester's law of inertia but not the isometry criterion.

name: The Rockafellar–Rüschendorf theorem
text: for an arbitrary real cost c on X × Y, every c-cyclically monotone set lies in the c-superdifferential of a c-concave potential, and conversely the contact set of a dual feasible pair is c-cyclically monotone; no measure or topology enters, and the measure-theoretic half of the Schachermayer–Teichmann optimality criterion is what remains (Rockafellar 1966; Villani, *Topics in Optimal Transportation*, §2.3).

name: Genus zero and genus one function fields
text: for F/k with exact constant field: in genus one with a divisor of degree one, each degree-one divisor is equivalent to exactly one degree-one place, and P ↦ [P − P₀] is a bijection from the degree-one places onto Cl⁰(F) whose transported addition satisfies P ⊕ Q = R ↔ P + Q ∼ R + P₀, the intrinsic group law of an elliptic function field, no Weierstrass equation needed, beside the E(F) ≅ Cl⁰(F(E)) of TauCeti#6497; and in genus zero with a divisor of degree one, F ≅ k(x) (Stichtenoth, Props 1.6.3, 6.1.6, 6.1.7).

name: The Riemann bilinear relations in weight one
text: for an effective Hodge structure of weight one with Weil operator C, a nondegenerate alternating integral form Q with Q(Cx, Cy) = Q(x, y) and Q(Cx, x) > 0 on nonzero real vectors is a polarization, and both relations are necessary, so they characterise the Riemann forms of a lattice with a complex structure (Voisin, *Hodge Theory I*, §7.1.2).

name: Stickelberger's congruence
text: the discriminant of every number field is ≡ 0 or 1 mod 4: with P and N the even and odd halves of the Leibniz expansion of the embedding determinant, P + N and PN are Galois-fixed algebraic integers and disc = (P + N)² − 4PN; Mathlib has this for quadratic fundamental discriminants only (Stickelberger 1897; Narkiewicz, Ch. 4).

name: The multivariate Gamma integral
text: ∫_(A > 0) det(A)^(a−(p+1)/2) e^(−tr A) dA = Γ_p(a) over the positive-definite p × p matrices for a > (p−1)/2, announced two days ago in dimension 0 only and now in every dimension: Lebesgue measure on the cone is the pushforward under L ↦ LLᵀ of Lebesgue measure on positive-diagonal lower-triangular L weighted by 2^p ∏ L_ii^(p−i); the Wishart normalising constant (Muirhead, Thms 2.1.9, 2.1.14).

name: Burnside's basis theorem for pro-p groups
text: a subset of a pro-p group G topologically generates G exactly when its image topologically generates G/Φ_p(G), since a proper closed subgroup lies in an open normal subgroup of index p; the theorem the Frattini subgroup Φ_p(G) of TauCeti#6649 exists for (Ribes–Zalesskii, §2.8).

name: Topologically finitely generated profinite groups are Hopfian
text: a continuous surjective endomorphism of such a group has trivial kernel and is a topological automorphism, by counting the open subgroups of each index; the shift on ∏_ℕ F shows finite generation cannot be dropped (Ribes–Zalesskii, *Profinite Groups*, Prop. 2.5.2).

name: A number field is discrete in its adele ring
text: the diagonal copy of K in 𝔸_K is a discrete closed subgroup and 𝔸_K/K is Hausdorff, the neighbourhood of 0 meeting K only in 0 being the adeles of norm < 1 at every infinite place and integral at every finite place; compactness of 𝔸_K/K is the next step (Cassels–Fröhlich, II §14).

name: Frobenius functionals and the Nakayama automorphism
text: a functional φ on a finite-dimensional algebra A with (a, b) ↦ φ(ab) nondegenerate, making A a Frobenius algebra: one exists exactly when A ≅ Hom_k(A, k) as right A-modules, the Nakayama automorphism ν with φ(ab) = φ(b ν(a)) is a unique algebra automorphism, trivial exactly when φ is symmetric, and A is injective as a left and as a right module over itself (Lam, *Lectures on Modules and Rings*, §16).

name: The quantile function and inverse transform sampling
text: F_μ⁻¹(t) = inf{x | t ≤ F_μ(x)} for a law μ on ℝ, and F_μ⁻¹ pushes the uniform law on (0, 1) forward to μ; reading two quantile functions off one uniform variable gives the monotone coupling of two real laws, whence W_p(μ, ν) ≤ ‖F_μ⁻¹ − F_ν⁻¹‖_(L^p(0,1)) for every p ∈ [1, ∞]; equality is still to come (Villani, §2.2).

name: Linear codes
text: a linear code as a subspace of Fⁿ presented by a generator matrix (row space) or a parity-check matrix (kernel), compatible exactly when HGᵀ = 0; monomial and permutation equivalence of codes, preserving Hamming weight, distance, dimension and weight distribution; and the Euclidean dual C^⊥ with (C^⊥)^⊥ = C, dim C + dim C^⊥ = n and #C · #C^⊥ = qⁿ (Huffman–Pless, §§1.2–1.6).

name: The Teichmüller lift of a local field
text: for a nonarchimedean local field with residue field 𝓀 of order q, the unique multiplicative section 𝓀ˣ → 𝒪ˣ of reduction with values in the (q−1)-torsion, whose image is exactly μ_(q−1), so reduction identifies μ_(q−1)(K) with 𝓀ˣ; built from Hensel's lemma via μₙ(R) ≅ μₙ(R/𝔪) for a Henselian local domain R with n invertible, unlike Mathlib's `Perfection.teichmuller` (Serre, *Corps Locaux*, II §4).

name: Clifford's theorem for function fields
text: for a function field of genus g with infinite exact constant field and a divisor D with 0 ≤ deg D ≤ 2g − 2, 2ℓ(D) ≤ deg D + 2, via ℓ(A) + ℓ(B) ≤ 1 + ℓ(A + B) for nonzero Riemann–Roch spaces; the finite-constant-field case waits on constant field extension (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Thm 1.6.13).

name: Hilbert 90 for infinite Galois extensions, and the Kummer isomorphism
text: for every Galois extension L/K, finite or infinite, the continuous cohomology H¹(Gal(L/K), Lˣ) vanishes, so H¹(G_K, (Kˢ)ˣ) = 0 and, for n invertible in K, a ↦ [g ↦ g(α)/α] with αⁿ = a is an isomorphism Kˣ/(Kˣ)ⁿ ≅ H¹(G_K, μₙ); Mathlib's finite-layer Hilbert 90 is the input at each finite level (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, *Cohomology of Number Fields*, 6.2.1).

name: The splitting criterion for quaternion algebras
text: over a field K with 2 invertible and a, b ∈ Kˣ, the following are equivalent: ℍ[K,a,b] ≅ M₂(K); b is a norm from K[T]/(T² − a); b = x² − ay² is solvable; ⟨1, −a, −b⟩ is isotropic; the norm form ⟨1, −a, −b, ab⟩ is isotropic; and every such algebra is either split or a division algebra (Lam, *Introduction to Quadratic Forms over Fields*, III.2.7, III.4.2; Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, III.1).

name: The Diaconis–Freedman representation, for every recurrent process
text: a recurrent Markov exchangeable process on a countable state space started at a fixed state is a mixture of Markov chains; the version announced for TauCeti#6231 needed every state to be visited almost surely, and that hypothesis is now gone by passing to the visited successor array (Diaconis–Freedman, *de Finetti's theorem for Markov chains*, Ann. Probab. 8 (1980)).

name: The Cartan matrix of an Artinian ring
text: over an Artinian ring R the indecomposable projective classes form a ℤ-basis of K₀(proj R) with Krull–Schmidt multiplicities as coordinates, the pairing ⟨[P_i], [M]⟩ = [M : S_i] against the simple-class basis of G₀(mod R) is perfect, the Cartan map has matrix C_ij = [P_j : S_i], and det C = ±1 whenever every finitely generated module has a finite projective resolution, Eilenberg's theorem, with the sign left open (Assem–Simson–Skowroński, *Elements of the Representation Theory of Associative Algebras I*, III.3).

name: Corestriction in group cohomology
text: for a subgroup S ≤ G of finite index, the transfer Hⁿ(S, Res A) → Hⁿ(G, A) in every degree, built through Shapiro's lemma and the trace Coind Res A → A, natural in A and with cor ∘ res = [G : S]; on the way Mathlib's Shapiro isomorphism is identified as restriction followed by evaluation at 1 (Brown, *Cohomology of Groups*, III §9).

name: The center of a semisimple group is finite
text: the scheme-theoretic center of a semisimple affine group scheme over a field is finite over that field, in every characteristic and with no reducedness assumption on the center, the finiteness input for the central isogeny onto the adjoint group (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*; Springer, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, §8.1).

name: The structure of the multiplicative group of a local field
text: for a nonarchimedean local field with residue field of order q, a uniformizer ϖ gives a topological isomorphism Kˣ ≅ ℤ × 𝒪ˣ, x ↦ (v(x), xϖ^(−v(x))), and the Teichmüller lift gives the canonical 𝒪ˣ ≅ μ_(q−1) × U⁽¹⁾, so Kˣ ≅ ℤ × μ_(q−1) × U⁽¹⁾ (Serre, *Corps Locaux*, II §§4–5; Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, II.5.3). Beside it, a finite extension of a nonarchimedean local field is again one, the spectral norm being its unique extended absolute value, and the containment half of the local square theorem: every unit of depth 2v(2) + 1 is a square, so (Kˣ)² is open, dyadic fields included (O'Meara, *Introduction to Quadratic Forms*, 63:1).

name: The smooth local geodesic flow
text: on a finite-dimensional boundaryless manifold, the maximal flow of a C^(n+1) vector field is jointly C^(n+1) in initial point and time near (x₀, 0), the local half of the fundamental theorem on flows, and the geodesic spray of a Riemannian manifold has a jointly smooth local flow on TM whose projections are the geodesics with prescribed initial data; the interface follows the open mathlib4#26394, and the global flow and exponential map come next (Lee, *Introduction to Smooth Manifolds*, Thm 9.12; do Carmo, *Riemannian Geometry*, Ch. 3 §2).

name: The function field of an elliptic curve has genus one
text: for an elliptic Weierstrass curve W over any field F, F(W) has genus one with exact constant field F, read off from L(n·O) = {p + qy : 2 deg p ≤ n, 2 deg q + 3 ≤ n} and Riemann's theorem; so Mathlib's elliptic curves are elliptic function fields in the sense of yesterday's TauCeti#6812 (Stichtenoth, Prop 6.1.3; Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, III.3).

name: The Kauffman bracket
