text: the state sum ⟨D⟩ = Σ_s a^(A(s)−B(s)) δ^(loops(s)−1), δ = −(a² + a⁻²), of a planar-diagram code, invariant under relabelling, the mirror image inverting a, ⟨c circles⟩ = δ^(c−1) and ⟨kink⟩ = −a³; invariance under the Reidemeister moves, and with it the Jones polynomial, is not yet there (Kauffman, *State models and the Jones polynomial*, Topology 26 (1987)).

name: Dedekind's theorem
text: for an algebraic integer θ whose minimal polynomial f over ℤ is squarefree mod p, an arithmetic Frobenius at a prime above p in a Galois number field splitting f permutes the roots of f with cycle type the degrees of the irreducible factors of f mod p, fixed roots counted as 1-cycles; in polynomial form, [for monic f ∈ ℤ[X] with p ∤ disc f, Gal(f) contains an element of exactly that cycle type](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Frobenius/CycleType.html#TauCeti.NumberField.exists_gal_fullCycleType_eq_factorizationType). On the way, a Frobenius and inertia generate the decomposition group at ramified primes too, extending TauCeti#5602 (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, I §8 Ex. 4–5).

name: Strong approximation for the finite adele ring
text: for any Dedekind domain R with fraction field K, K is dense in the finite adele ring 𝔸_K^f: an element of K approximates a given finite adele at finitely many places while staying integral elsewhere, so 𝔸_K^f = K + ∏ 𝒪_v; Mathlib has the matching density at the infinite places of a number field (Cassels–Fröhlich, *Algebraic Number Theory*, II §15).

name: Dedekind's different theorem, both halves
text: for a finite separable extension of algebraic function fields and a place P′ over P, d(P′|P) = e(P′|P) − 1 exactly when P′ is tame (separable residue extension, e prime to the residue characteristic) and d ≥ e exactly when it is wild, without assuming a perfect constant field; the tame direction was TauCeti#5807, and underneath is P^e ∣ 𝔡(B/A) iff the residue extension at P is inseparable or e vanishes in A/p, where Mathlib has P ∣ 𝔡 iff ramified and P^(e−1) ∣ 𝔡 (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Thm 3.5.1, Cor 3.5.5).

name: The Poincaré–Wirtinger inequality for C¹ functions on a convex domain
text: for Ω bounded convex open in an n-dimensional real normed space with Haar measure, S ⊆ Ω of positive measure, u ∈ C¹(Ω) and 1 ≤ p < ∞, ‖u − ⨍_S u‖_{Lᵖ(Ω)} ≤ |B(0,1)| (diam Ω)^(n+1) / |S| · ‖Du‖_{Lᵖ(Ω)}, via Schur's test for integral operators, also new; the constant is not sharp, and the W^{1,p} version waits on Meyers–Serrin (Gilbarg–Trudinger, (7.45)).

name: The Weyl module 𝕊^μ(kⁿ) is an irreducible representation of GLₙ(k)
text: in characteristic zero, the image of a Young symmetrizer of shape μ on (kⁿ)^{⊗|μ|} is irreducible under GLₙ(k) exactly when μ has at most n rows, so the Schur functor of TauCeti#1751 takes simple values there, by an annihilator comparison in k[S_d] and Schur–Weyl duality (Fulton–Harris, *Representation Theory*, Thm 6.3).

name: Atkin–Lehner operators commute with the good Hecke operators
text: for Q ∥ N the normalized involution 𝒲_Q on M_k(Γ₀(N)) and on S_k(Γ₀(N)) commutes with the Hecke operator of every Γ₀(N) double coset whose determinant is coprime to Q, since the Atkin–Lehner matrix normalizes Γ₀(N) and fixes each such double coset; the identification with the classical Tₙ is next (Atkin–Lehner, Math. Ann. 185 (1970); Shimura, §3.4).

name: The Frobenius trace at bad reduction is 1, −1 or 0
text: over the fraction field of a DVR with residue field of size q, the trace a = q + 1 − #W̃(𝔽_q) of the reduction of a minimal Weierstrass equation, singular point included, is 1, −1, 0 at split multiplicative, nonsplit multiplicative and additive reduction in every characteristic, so Mathlib's case-defined local polynomial is 1 − aT + qT² at good and 1 − aT at bad reduction (Silverman, *AEC*, VII.5, App. C.16).

name: Dedekind's criterion
text: for an integral primitive element θ with f = minpoly ℤ θ and f ≡ ∏ φᵢ^{eᵢ} mod p, write f − ∏ Φᵢ^{eᵢ} = pH for lifts Φᵢ; then p ∤ [𝓞_K : ℤ[θ]] exactly when for every i either eᵢ = 1 or φᵢ ∤ H mod p, independently of the lifts. Beside it, p stays prime in the Dedekind–Kummer setting exactly when the minimal polynomial is irreducible mod p, closing a TODO in Mathlib (Cohen, *A Course in Computational Algebraic Number Theory*, Thm 6.1.4).

name: The Hilbert symbol
text: (a, b) = +1 or −1 according as b = x² − a y² is solvable, over any field; with 2 invertible it is +1 exactly when the quaternion algebra (a, b) splits, equivalently when ⟨1, −a, −b⟩ is isotropic; it is symmetric and depends only on square classes (Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, III §1; Lam, III.2.7).

name: Eisenstein series with character
text: for Dirichlet characters ψ mod u and φ mod v, weight k ≥ 3 and uv ∣ N, G_k^{ψ,φ}(z) = Σ_{(c,d)} ψ(c) φ⁻¹(d) (cvz + d)^(−k) is a modular form for Γ₁(N) lying in the nebentypus space M_k(N, ψφ), zero unless ψ(−1)φ(−1) = (−1)^k; the normalization E_k^{ψ,φ} and its q-expansion come next (Diamond–Shurman, *A First Course in Modular Forms*, §4.5).

name: Linear codes: generator and parity-check matrices, minimum distance, weight enumerators

reference.text: Voyager, TauCeti#6778, TauCeti#6869, TauCeti#7337, TauCeti#6873, TauCeti#7160, TauCeti#7195

text: codes generated and checked by matrices, with rank formulas and [I | A] against [−Aᵀ | I]; the minimum Hamming distance as the least nonzero weight of an additive code; the weight enumerator W_C(X, Y) = Σ_w A_w X^(n−w) Y^w, multiplicative on direct sums; duals of punctured and shortened codes, Hermitian duality and information sets, with the MacWilliams identity next; minimum distance is also being formalised in mathlib4#38014 (Huffman–Pless, *Fundamentals of Error-Correcting Codes*, Ch. 1, §7.2).

name: Riemann–Roch for a proper curve
text: χ(𝒪_X(D)) = dim H⁰ − dim H¹ = deg D + 1 − g for a Weil divisor on a proper integral curve with a rational point and discrete valuation rings in codimension one, with deg D = Σ_y D(y)·[κ(y):k] and g = dim_k H¹(X, 𝒪_X); finite-dimensionality of H¹ is still a hypothesis, and Serre duality is not there yet (Hartshorne IV.1.3).

name: The Weyl character formula
text: ch(M)·∏_{α>0}(1 − e^(−α)) = Σ_{w∈W} sgn(w)·e^(w·λ) for a finite-dimensional module generated by a highest-weight vector of weight λ over a Lie algebra with non-degenerate Killing form in characteristic zero, proved with no order on the scalars, chamber arguments replaced by inversion sets (Humphreys §24).

name: The Wiener–Ikehara theorem
text: for nonnegative coefficients whose Dirichlet series converges on Re s > 1 and differs from κ/(s − 1) by a function continuous on Re s ≥ 1, x⁻¹·Σ_{n ≤ x} a(n) → κ, with the natural-cutoff and shifted-abscissa variants (Korevaar, *Tauberian Theory*, Ch. III).

name: The Hurwitz genus formula
text: [k′:k]·(2g′ − 2) = [F′:F]·(2g − 2) + [k′:k]·deg Diff(F′/F) for a finite separable extension of function fields, from the cotrace identity (Cotr ω) = Con(ω) + Diff, with the tame bound and its equality criterion, g ≤ g′, and ramification of every extension of k(x) of degree above one when k is the full constant field (Stichtenoth 3.4.13).

name: The binary Golay codes
text: the extended [24, 12, 8] code of the generator [I₁₂ | B], self-dual and doubly even, enumerator X²⁴ + 759X¹⁶Y⁸ + 2576X¹²Y¹² + 759X⁸Y¹⁶ + Y²⁴, and its [23, 12, 7] puncture at every coordinate, recovered by the parity extension; every finite check is a kernel computation (Conway–Sloane, Ch. 3).

name: The MacWilliams identity
text: #C·W_{C⊥}(X, Y) = W_C(X + (q − 1)Y, X − Y) in ℤ[X, Y] for a linear code over a field of q elements, with the Krawtchouk form #C·A_w(C⊥) = Σ_j A_j(C)·K_w(j) (MacWilliams–Sloane, Ch. 5).

name: Morrey's inequality and the Morrey embedding
text: for p > n a C¹ function with Lᵖ derivative is Hölder of exponent 1 − n/p with an explicit constant, every u ∈ W^(1,p)(ℝⁿ) agrees a.e. with such a function, and the induced map into C^(0,1−n/p)(ℝⁿ) is bounded and injective; the borderline p = n is open (Evans §5.6).

name: Marcinkiewicz interpolation
text: between two finite endpoints: a subadditive operator of weak type (p₀, p₀) and (p₁, p₁) is of strong type (p, p) for p₀ < p < p₁, with explicit constants degenerating at each end (Stein–Weiss, Ch. V).

name: The Herglotz representation theorem
text: a function holomorphic on the unit disc has nonnegative real part exactly when it is w ↦ ∫ (z + w)/(z − w) dμ(z) + i·Im F(0) for a finite measure on the circle, built on Mathlib's Poisson and Herglotz–Riesz kernels (Duren, Ch. 1).

name: The Schwarz–Christoffel mapping theorem, convex case
text: for ordered prevertices with exponents in (−1, 0) summing to −2 the primitive maps the upper half-plane bijectively onto the polygon's interior, by showing it is a covering map off the boundary path; the non-convex case and the parameter problem remain (Driscoll–Trefethen, Ch. 2).

name: Metric completeness gives geodesic completeness
text: in a Riemannian manifold complete for its Riemannian distance every maximal geodesic is defined for all time, so the exponential map is defined on the whole tangent space; this is one arrow of Hopf–Rinow, not the equivalence (do Carmo 7.2.8).

name: The Grothendieck–Witt and Witt rings of a field
text: GW(K) as the Grothendieck ring of regular quadratic forms and W(K) as its quotient by the hyperbolic ideal, two forms having the same Witt class exactly when their anisotropic parts are isometric (Lam II §1).

name: Dedekind's theorem on factorization modulo primes
text: at a prime not dividing the discriminant the Galois image contains an element whose cycle type is the factorization type of f mod p, with the criteria that then give Aₙ and Sₙ, worked on x⁵ − x − 1; the transitive subgroups of Sₙ are classified for n ≤ 5 too, and an irreducible cubic has group A₃ or S₃ by its discriminant (van der Waerden §61).

name: The Fricke functional equation and the Atkin–Lehner sign
text: Λ_N(k − s, f) = i^k·Λ_N(s, g) for the completed L-function; a newform of trivial nebentypus has Fricke eigenvalue ±1; and Tₙ* = χ(n)⁻¹Tₙ on S_k(N, χ) for (n, N) = 1 (Diamond–Shurman §5.10).

name: The class group of a curve is its Picard group
text: every line bundle on a Noetherian integral scheme of dimension at most one with discrete valuation rings in codimension one is the sheaf 𝒪_X(D) of a Weil divisor, so Cl(X) → Pic(X) is an isomorphism (Hartshorne II.6.16).

name: The Caccioppoli inequality
text: ∫ψ²‖∇u‖² ≤ (2Λ/λ)²∫‖∇ψ‖²u² + (2/λ)∫ψ²fu for a weak solution of a divergence-form uniformly elliptic equation, with constants depending only on the ellipticity bounds (Gilbarg–Trudinger, Ch. 8).

name: The Clifford correspondence, irreducibility half
text: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, inducing to G an irreducible representation of the inertia group of an irreducible representation of a normal subgroup gives an irreducible one; the bijection is still to come (Isaacs 6.11).

name: Multiplicativity of the Herbrand quotient
text: the quotient announced with TauCeti#5764 is multiplicative in a short exact sequence of representations of a finite cyclic group, by the exact hexagon of Tate cohomology, and unchanged by a map with finite kernel and cokernel (Neukirch IV §7).

name: Class formations and their fundamental classes
text: the Artin–Tate axioms in finite-layer form, with H²(K/F) cyclic of order [K:F] generated by the class of invariant 1/[K:F], and the hypotheses of Tate's theorem available for every subgroup; reciprocity is not claimed (Artin–Tate XIV).

name: Dummit's solvability criterion for quintics
text: a monic irreducible separable quintic over any field has solvable Galois group if and only if its F₂₀ resolvent sextic has a root in the base field, provided that sextic is separable (Dummit, *Solving solvable quintics*, Math. Comp. 57 (1991), Thm 1); it rests on the general resolvent root criterion, that the resolvent for H ≤ Sₙ has a root in F exactly when the Galois image is conjugate into H (Cohen §6.3), and on a transitive subgroup of S₅ being solvable iff it lies in a conjugate of F₂₀.

name: Kostant's multiplicity formula
text: dim M_μ = Σ_{w∈W} sgn(w)·P(w(λ+ρ) − (μ+ρ)) for a finite-dimensional module generated by a highest-weight vector of weight λ over a Lie algebra with non-degenerate Killing form in characteristic zero, P the Kostant partition function, read off from the Weyl character formula of TauCeti#7644 by dividing by the Weyl denominator coefficient by coefficient (Humphreys §24.2, Kostant 1959); the statement for the irreducible L(λ) itself waits on the injectivity half of PBW.

name: Mixed Hodge structures form an abelian category
text: with rational Hodge morphisms, assembled from binary products with componentwise weight and Hodge filtrations (new here) and the kernels, cokernels and coimage–image comparison that strictness (TauCeti#4782) provided (Deligne, *Théorie de Hodge II*, 2.3.5).

name: Weierstrass division for restricted power series
text: over a complete nonarchimedean field, if f is restricted and distinguished of degree s at a radius c (its Gauss norm at c is attained in degree s and every later coefficient is strictly smaller), every restricted series g is uniquely g = q·f + r with q restricted and r a polynomial of degree below s; existence lands here and, with the norm identity and uniqueness of TauCeti#7664, completes Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert §5.2.1 Thm 2. Mathlib's `PowerSeries.IsWeierstrassDivisionAt` is the adic-order variant, and neither statement implies the other.

name: Lattice-point counting with a boundary-order error
text: for a ℤ-lattice L in an n-dimensional real normed space, a Haar measure μ and a bounded set D whose frontier is Lipschitz parametrizable in dimension n − 1, #(c·D ∩ L) = μ(D)/covol(L) · cⁿ + O(c^(n−1)) as c → ∞, from a cell decomposition and the count #((c·S + B) ∩ L) ≤ A·c^d for S Lipschitz parametrizable in dimension d (Lang, *Algebraic Number Theory* VI §2); Mathlib's `ZLattice.covolume.tendsto_card_div_pow'` gives the leading term with no error.

name: Every graphon is representable on the unit interval
text: a graphon on an arbitrary probability space is at cut distance zero from a graphon on ([0, 1], Lebesgue): joint measurability lets it factor as W(x, y) = V(q(x), q(y)) through a measurable map q to the Cantor space, so it is a pullback from a standard Borel carrier (Janson, *Graphons, cut norm and distance*, Thm 7.1 and Lemma 7.3).

name: The Nevanlinna representation of Pick functions
text: a function holomorphic on the upper half-plane with nonnegative imaginary part is F(z) = b·z + ∫_ℝ (1 + xz)/(x − z) dρ(x) + Re F(i) with b ≥ 0 and ρ a finite positive measure on ℝ, obtained from the Herglotz representation of TauCeti#7513 by the Cayley map z ↦ (z − i)/(z + i) and the boundary Cayley homeomorphism ℝ ≃ S¹ ∖ {1}, splitting off the atom at 1 (Schilling–Song–Vondraček, *Bernstein Functions*, Ch. 6).

name: The semi-local decomposition at a finite place
text: for an extension L/K of number fields and a finite place v of K, K_v ⊗_K L ≅ ∏_{w ∣ v} L_w as K_v-algebras with a ⊗ x ↦ (a·x)_w, hence [Σ_{w ∣ v} [L_w : K_v] = [L : K]](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/LocalGlobal/Semilocal/Basic.html#TauCeti.sum_finrank_adicCompletion_eq_finrank), the finite-place counterpart of Mathlib's `NumberField.InfinitePlace.sum_inertiaDeg_eq_finrank` (Neukirch II (8.3)).

name: Shimizu's lemma
text: if a discrete subgroup Γ ≤ PSL(2, ℝ) contains the translation z ↦ z + w, every element of Γ with lower-left entry c ≠ 0 has |c| ≥ |w|⁻¹, equivalently (g·z).im · z.im ≤ w² whenever g ∈ Γ does not fix ∞ (Jørgensen's proof, Beardon §5.4); hence horodiscs of height at least the cusp width are precisely invariant under the cusp stabilizer.

name: A separable isogeny is unramified
text: for a separable isogeny φ of elliptic curves, every place of the source function field is unramified over the target, since both have genus one and the Hurwitz formula forces the different to vanish; hence Σ_{P′ ∣ P} f(P′ ∣ P) = deg φ, and over a separably closed constant field every place has exactly deg φ places above it (Silverman II.5.9, III.4.10).

name: Construction A and the Golay lattice
text: the Construction A lattice of a code C ≤ (ℤ/m)ⁿ is even exactly when 2m ∣ Σ zᵢ² for every integer lift of a codeword (for m = 2: C doubly even), its discriminant is mⁿ/#C² for self-orthogonal C, and for the extended binary Golay code of TauCeti#7570 it is a positive-definite even unimodular lattice of rank 24 (Ebeling §1.3, Conway–Sloane Ch. 7).

name: The fundamental ideal of the Witt ring
text: I(K) = ker(dim mod 2) on the Witt ring of TauCeti#7604 is generated as an additive group by the one-fold Pfister classes ⟨⟨a⟩⟩ = ⟨1, −a⟩ (Lam, Ch. II §1).

name: Scalar curvature
text: the basis-free metric trace of the Ricci tensor of a connection on a Riemannian tangent bundle, with its orthonormal-basis, Einstein and constant-curvature formulas, n(n − 1)κ when R(w, u)v = κ(⟨u, v⟩w − ⟨w, v⟩u) (Lee, *Introduction to Riemannian Manifolds*, Ch. 7).

name: The minimal discriminant ideal
text: 𝔇_{E/K} = ∏ᵥ 𝔭ᵥ^(v(Δ_min,v)) for an elliptic curve over the fraction field of a Dedekind domain O, a finite nonzero product invariant under change of variables, and for an equation integral over O equal to (Δ) exactly when the equation is globally minimal (Silverman VIII.8).

name: Unramified extensions of local fields
text: for an extension L/K of nonarchimedean local fields, e(L/K) = 1 with separable residue extension (automatic here), shown equivalent to v_L ∘ ι = v_K, to 𝔪_K 𝒪_L = 𝔪_L, to f(L/K) = [L : K], stable in towers in both directions, and identified with Mathlib's `Algebra.FormallyUnramified 𝒪[K] 𝒪[L]` (Serre, *Corps Locaux* I §4, III §5).

name: The Weyl dimension formula
text: for a finite-dimensional module M generated by a highest-weight vector of weight λ over a Lie algebra with non-degenerate Killing form in characteristic zero, dim M = ∏_{α>0} ⟨λ+ρ, α^∨⟩ / ⟨ρ, α^∨⟩, specialised from the Weyl character formula of TauCeti#7644 (Humphreys §24.3); the statement for L(λ) at every dominant integral λ still waits on the injectivity half of PBW.

name: The first Bianchi identity
text: R(u,v)w + R(v,w)u + R(w,u)v = 0 for the curvature of any torsion-free smooth connection on the tangent bundle, in any finite dimension, boundary allowed, no metric needed (Lee, *Riemannian Manifolds*, Ch. 7).

name: The functional equation of a newform, with its sign
text: for a newform f of weight k and trivial nebentypus, Λ_N(k − s, f) = i^k ε_N(f) Λ_N(s, f) with ε_N(f) the Fricke sign, the two-form Fricke equation announced earlier collapsed to one form; the sign i^k ε_N(f) is ±1, and when it is −1 the L-function vanishes at s = k/2, so the analytic rank is positive (Diamond–Shurman Thm 5.10.2).

name: 𝔸_K/K is compact
text: for a number field K the quotient of the adele ring by the diagonal copy of K is compact, via a compact set of representatives from strong approximation and the Minkowski parallelepiped (Cassels–Fröhlich II §14); the adeles, ideles and idele class group are now locally compact Hausdorff as well (TauCeti#7920, TauCeti#7922).

name: A simultaneous Petersson-orthonormal Hecke eigenbasis
text: every fixed-nebentypus cusp space S_k(N, χ) has a finite basis, orthonormal for the Petersson product, whose vectors are eigenforms for every T_n with gcd(n, N) = 1, resting on the good T_n being normal with Petersson adjoint ⟨n⟩⁻¹T_n (Diamond–Shurman Thm 5.5.4).

name: The decomposition group is the local Galois group
text: for L/K Galois and a place w of L over a finite place v of K, continuous extension to the completions is an isomorphism D_w ≅ Gal(L_w/K_v), so L_w/K_v is Galois, cyclic of order f when w is unramified, and the global arithmetic Frobenius at w extends to the local one (Neukirch II §9); locally, reduction gives Gal(L/K) ≅ Gal(𝓀_L/𝓀_K) for unramified extensions of local fields (TauCeti#7860).

name: The adic spectrum of A⟨T/s⟩ is the rational subset
text: for a Huber ring A, pullback along A → A⟨T/s⟩ is a homeomorphism Spa(A⟨T/s⟩, A_U⁺) ≃ R(T/s) (Wedhorn, *Adic Spaces*, Prop. 8.2(2), first assertion), built on Spa(Â, Â⁺) ≃ Spa(A, A⁺) for the completion, matching rational subsets (Prop. 7.48, TauCeti#7848, TauCeti#7913); the two-piece Laurent case of Tate acyclicity (Lemma 8.33) landed alongside (TauCeti#7877).

name: The small-chains theorem
text: for an open cover U of a space X, the inclusion of the singular chains subordinate to U into all singular chains is a chain homotopy equivalence with a strict retraction, hence an isomorphism on singular homology (Hatcher Prop. 2.21), the input to excision.

name: The Galois correspondence for normal extensions
text: for E/F normal but not necessarily separable, Gal(E/F) is profinite and its closed subgroups correspond to the intermediate fields of the separable closure of F in E. Mathlib has the infinite Galois correspondence for Galois extensions; this is its extension to imperfect base fields, which also makes the absolute Galois group profinite.

name: H² regularity of whole-space weak solutions
text: for a constant uniformly elliptic matrix A, a weak solution u ∈ H¹(ℝⁿ) of −∂ⱼ(Aⁱʲ∂ᵢu) = f with f ∈ L² lies in H²(ℝⁿ), with ‖∂_w∂_y u‖_{L²} ≤ ‖y‖‖w‖‖f‖_{L²}/λ, by difference quotients (Evans §6.3.1 Thm 1); interior estimates and variable coefficients are the next steps.

name: Local monogenicity
text: a discrete valuation ring S, finite over a discrete valuation subring R with separable residue extension, is R[β] for a single β, with the resulting integral power basis (Serre, *Corps Locaux* III §6 Prop. 12); Mathlib has the unramified case, and this covers tame and wild ramification without assuming completeness.

name: Type II codes have length divisible by eight
text: a doubly-even self-dual binary code has 8 ∣ n, from the MacWilliams identity and the symmetry W(X, iY) = W(X, Y) of its weight enumerator (Huffman–Pless Ch. 9).

name: The primitive quadratic character of a fundamental discriminant
text: a fundamental discriminant D defines a Dirichlet character of level |D|, the product of the characters of its prime discriminants; it is primitive and equals the Legendre symbol (D/q) at every odd prime q (Ireland–Rosen Ch. 6).

name: The chain rule and truncation in W^{1,p}(Ω)
text: for Lipschitz C¹ F with F(0) = 0, F ∘ u ∈ W^{1,p} with ∇(F ∘ u) = F′(u)∇u, and u⁺ ∈ W^{1,p} with ∇u⁺ = 1_{u>0}∇u (Gilbarg–Trudinger Lemma 7.6); the Poincaré–Wirtinger inequality, announced earlier for C¹ functions, now holds on W^{1,p}(Ω) for bounded convex Ω with the same constant (TauCeti#7843).

name: Differential graded categories
text: categories enriched in cochain complexes of R-modules, with the homogeneous-morphism calculus and the graded Leibniz rule d(fg) = (df)g + (−1)^{|f|} f(dg), compared with Mathlib's Hom complexes of cochain complexes (Keller, *Deriving DG categories*); the DG Yoneda lemma for the free rank-one right module came with it (TauCeti#7912).

name: The free profinite group
text: the profinite completion of the free group on a type X, with its universal property, that a map from X into a profinite group extends uniquely to a continuous homomorphism; functorial in X and unique up to unique isomorphism (Ribes–Zalesskii Ch. 3).

name: The two-dimensional Ginzburg DG algebra
text: Π₂(Q) for a finite quiver Q: the doubled path algebra with a degree −1 loop t_i at each vertex and d(t_i) the preprojective relator ρ_i, with d² = 0 and bidegree (1, 0) (Ginzburg, *Calabi–Yau algebras* §4.2; Keller, *Deformed Calabi–Yau completions* §6.5); H⁰(Π₂(Q)) ≅ Π(Q) is the next step.

name: Pic⁰ of a curve
text: on a proper integral curve, the Euler-characteristic degree deg L = χ(L) − χ(𝒪_X) is a homomorphism Pic X → ℤ, its kernel Pic⁰ X is degree-zero divisors modulo principal divisors, and a point of residue degree one gives Pic X / Pic⁰ X ≅ ℤ (Hartshorne II.6, IV.1).

name: Spectrality of the adic spectrum
text: `Spa(A,A⁺)` is a spectral space for a Huber ring and a ring of integral elements, by the characterisation of the continuous locus inside `Spv(A,IA)`.

name: Wedhorn's completion theorem (Proposition 7.48)
text: pullback along `A → Â` is [a homeomorphism `Spa(Â,Â⁺) ≃ Spa(A,A⁺)`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Spa/Completion/Homeomorph.html#TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaCompletionHomeomorph), for `Â⁺` the closure of the image of `A⁺`, and it matches rational subsets.

name: Faithful flatness along a rational cover (Corollary 8.32)
text: for a finite rational cover of `Spa(A,A⁺)`, the map from `A` into the product of the coordinate rings is faithfully flat, so in particular injective: Čech exactness in degree zero.

name: Exactness for the two-piece Laurent cover (Lemma 8.33)
text: a pair of sections over `{|f| ≤ 1}` and `{|f| ≥ 1}` agreeing on the overlap is a pair of equal constants, and the differential onto the overlap is surjective. This is proved for the quotient presentations of the coordinate rings, not for presheaf sections.

name: Weierstrass division
text: over a complete nonarchimedean field, a restricted series distinguished of degree `s` at a positive radius divides every restricted series in exactly one way. One variable only.

name: The completed rational localisation with its plus ring
text: `A_U⁺` is the closure of the integral closure of `A⁺[T/s]`, and [`(A⟨T/s⟩, A_U⁺)` is a Huber pair](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/LocalizationTopology/Plus.html#TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.isRingOfIntegralElements_completedPlusSubring). name: The Riemann–Roch theorem

name: The suspended and unsuspended Stasheff identities agree

name: Normalization of contractions

name: Artin–Whaples weak approximation at mixed places
text: for finite sets of finite and infinite places, the diagonal image of a number field is dense in the product of the corresponding completions; this is the load-bearing export to Global Quadratic Forms, in exactly the mixed form that roadmap requires.

name: Normalized absolute value on an infinite completion
text: the monoid-with-zero homomorphism `x ↦ ‖x‖ ^ w.mult` on `w.Completion`, giving `|x|` at a real place and `|z|²` at a complex place, continuous and vanishing only at zero; it supplies the archimedean half of the local absolute values that the product formula and the idele norm will need.

name: Agreement with the global normalized value on `K`
text: on the dense copy of `K` the completion value is the normalized infinite-place value, which is what lets statements about `K` transfer to the completion.

name: Resolution theorem
text: for a property `P` of `E`-projectives containing zero and closed under biproducts, the inclusion of `P` into the objects of finite `P`-dimension induces an isomorphism on exact K₀, with inverse the alternating class of any finite resolution.

name: Euler–Poincaré theorem
text: in abelian K₀ the alternating class of the terms of a bounded cochain complex equals that of its cohomology, for any short-exact-additive invariant.

name: Horseshoe lemma
text: in any exact category, resolutions of a conflation's outer terms, the right one projective, combine to resolve its middle term; with Schanuel's lemma this lifts finite projective resolutions along conflations.

name: Ext-Euler pairing
text: for extension-closed properties whose pairs are Euler-admissible, `χ(X,Y) = ∑ (-1)ⁿ dim Extⁿ(X,Y)` descends to the unique biadditive pairing on the two exact K₀ groups.

name: Laurent normalisation of the shift

name: The Hodge decomposition
text: the components H^{p,n−p} = F^p ∩ conj F^{n−p} of a bounded n-opposed filtration form an internal direct sum, and conversely (Deligne's equivalence, `decompositionEquiv`).

name: Semisimplicity of polarizable rational Hodge structures
text: every rational Hodge substructure of a polarizable pure Hodge structure has a complement over ℚ and after complexification, orthogonal for some polarizing form; proved via the Weil operator and the positive-definite Hodge form.

name: Deligne's theorem on the bigrading
text: the pieces I^{p,q}, defined by Deligne's closed formula in F, conj F and W, form an internal direct sum of the complex space, recovering W_k as ⨆_{p+q≤k} I^{p,q} and F^p as ⨆_{p'≥p} I^{p',q'}.

name: Strictness of morphisms of mixed Hodge structures
text: a morphism is strict for the Hodge filtration, range f ⊓ F'^p = f(F^p), and likewise for the rational and the complexified weight filtrations.

name: The Hodge numbers partition the dimension
text: ∑ h^{p,n−p} = dim_ℂ V_ℂ, equal to the lattice rank, with Hodge symmetry h^{p,q} = h^{q,p}.

name: do Carmo's distance is Mathlib's distance
text: the infimum of lengths over piecewise-`C¹` paths equals `Manifold.riemannianEDist`, via a corner-smoothing theorem giving every piecewise-`C¹` path a `C¹` path of the same endpoints and length.

name: Geodesics have constant speed
text: on an open preconnected parameter set a geodesic has the same speed at every two parameters, the lemma that makes a geodesic Cauchy at a finite endpoint.

name: The finite-endpoint extension criterion
text: an integral curve of a `C¹` vector field on `Ioo a b` that accumulates at a point of the manifold as `t → b⁻` extends past `b`, with the left-endpoint analogue; hence the maximal integral curve has no cluster point at a finite endpoint.

name: The Weil–Cartier equivalence
text: on a Noetherian integral curve whose codimension-one local rings are discrete valuation rings, Weil divisors and Cartier divisors are additively equivalent.

name: Locally principal divisors give line bundles
text: the sheaf `𝒪_X(D)` of a locally principal Weil divisor on such a curve is locally free of rank one.

name: `Pic⁰` as a quotient
text: degree-zero divisors modulo principal divisors form the degree-zero divisor class group, with every class represented in degree zero; this is only an abstract group.

name: Additivity of the curve Euler characteristic
text: `dim H⁰-dim H¹` is additive in a short exact sequence when the stated finite-dimensionality hypotheses hold and the relevant `H²` vanishes.

name: Commutativity of abelian varieties
text: a proper geometrically integral group scheme over a field is a commutative group object.

name: The Atkin–Lehner Main Lemma
text: a cusp form in `S_k(Γ₁(N), χ)` whose Fourier coefficients vanish at every index coprime to `N` is old, indeed a sum `∑_{p ∣ N} V_p f_p` of prime degeneracy images: mem_cuspFormsOld_of_forall_coprime_qExpansion_coeff_eq_zero. Stated per character space only.

name: Multiplicity one
text: a simultaneous eigenspace of the good Hecke operators in the new part of `S_k(N, χ)` is a line once nonzero: finrank_cuspFormsNewEigenspace_eq_one.

text: two newforms of the same level, weight and nebentypus whose eigenvalues agree at all good indices outside a finite set are equal: Newform.eq_of_forall_notMem_eigenvalue_eq. The cross-level version is not proved.

name: The general-level valence formula

name: The rational-radicand splitting law
text: away from the radicands' numerator and denominator primes, a rational prime splits completely exactly when every radicand is a quadratic residue. Lean declaration

name: The genus-field maximality theorem
text: for an imaginary quadratic base, the prime-discriminant compositum is maximal among abelian-over-ℚ extensions unramified at every place. Lean declaration

name: Genus characters

name: The unrestricted Artin map
text: fractional ideals map directly to Frobenius automorphisms in everywhere-unramified abelian extensions, supplying the reciprocity interface. Definition

name: Dedekind's theorem
text: the multiset of degrees of the monic irreducible factors of `minpoly ℤ θ` modulo `p` is the cycle type of a Frobenius at a prime above `p` acting on the roots of `minpoly ℚ θ`, with one part `1` restored for each fixed root.

name: Dedekind's criterion
text: the factorization of `minpoly ℤ θ` modulo `p` decides whether `p` divides the index `[𝓞 K : ℤ[θ]]`.

name: The double-coset splitting law
text: for `M/K` Galois with group `G` and `E` the fixed field of `H ≤ G`, the primes of `𝓞 E` above `p` are indexed by `H \ G / D`.

name: Stickelberger's congruence
text: the discriminant of a number field is `0` or `1` modulo `4`.

name: Ramification is the support of the relative discriminant
text: a nonzero prime divides it exactly when some prime above it is ramified, with no separability hypothesis on residue fields.

name: The Hille–Yosida characterization
text: a densely defined real Banach-space operator generates a C₀ semigroup of growth `(M, ω)` exactly when `(ω, ∞)` lies in its resolvent set and all resolvent powers satisfy the sharp bounds `‖R(λ,A)ⁿ‖ ≤ M/(λ−ω)ⁿ`.

name: The Lumer–Phillips characterization
text: an operator generates a contraction semigroup exactly when it is densely defined and maximally dissipative.

name: The Hausdorff–Bernstein–Widder theorem
text: closed-half-line complete monotonicity is equivalent to representation as the Laplace transform of a finite positive measure on `ℝ≥0`.

name: Bochner’s theorem
text: continuity and positive-definiteness on a finite-dimensional real inner-product space are equivalent to representation by a unique finite Borel measure under the project’s Fourier convention.

name: The Berg–Christensen–Ressel representation
text: every bounded continuous positive-definite function on the involutive semigroup `ℝ≥0 × V` has a unique finite Laplace–Fourier representing measure.

name: Primal attainment on Polish spaces
text: a lower semicontinuous cost `c : X × Y → ℝ≥0∞` admits an optimal plan between any two probability measures on Polish spaces, and the optimal plans form a compact set.

name: Stability of optimal transport

name: Rellich-Kondrachov
text: for bounded `Ω` and `1 ≤ p < ∞`, the value map `W^{1,p}_0(Ω) → Lᵖ(Ω)` is compact, by a Fréchet-Kolmogorov criterion. This is the compactness that powers everything spectral; the `W^{1,p}(Ω)` statement, which needs boundary regularity, is not available.

name: The weak maximum principle for second-order elliptic operators
text: a `C²` function on a compact set with `c u ≤ Δu + b·∇u`, `c ≥ 0` and `b` bounded inside, is bounded by any nonnegative bound it respects on the frontier, with a counterexample showing `c ≥ 0` cannot be dropped.

name: The Hardy-Littlewood maximal inequality
text: the weak `(1,1)` bound, and by Marcinkiewicz interpolation against `L^∞` the strong `(p, p)` bound for `1 < p < ∞`.

name: Full cycles in prime degree

name: Double transitivity from a long cycle

name: Shapiro's lemma in degrees 0 and 1
text: for profinite `G` and closed `U`, evaluation at `1` is an isomorphism `H¹(G, Coind_U^G A) ≃+ H¹(U, A)`, with inverse a section formula for any continuous coset factorization.

name: The low-degree long exact sequence
text: a short exact sequence of discrete `G`-modules over any topological group gives `δ⁰`, `δ¹` and exactness at all eight nodes from `H⁰(G, A)` to `H²(G, B)`.

name: `cor ∘ res = (G : U)` in degrees 0, 1 and 2
text: corestriction along a finite-index open subgroup, independent of the transversal by an explicit coboundary, satisfies the index identity on cohomology with its correction terms named.

name: The low-degree cup products
text: the six shapes with `p + q ≤ 2`, associativity in all ten tridegrees, graded commutativity on classes, and the projection formula in every shape.

name: The discrete-module dictionary

name: The finite-quotient system

name: Limit description of a profinite group
text: a compatible family of elements of the finite quotients of `G` comes from a unique element of `G`, stated outside the category so that later layers can consume it.

name: Correspondence theorem for open normal subgroups
text: the open normal subgroups of `G ⧸ N` correspond, as lattices, to the open normal subgroups of `G` containing `N`.

name: Universal property of the profinite completion
text: continuous homomorphisms from the completion of `G` to a profinite group correspond to abstract homomorphisms from `G`, with the unit bijective when `G` is finite.

name: Quotients by closed normal subgroups are totally disconnected

name: Open normal subgroups separate points
text: in a profinite group the intersection of the open normal subgroups is trivial.

name: The pro-`p` predicate
text: `IsProP` says every quotient by an open normal subgroup is a `p`-group; it is the carrier that Layer 2's Sylow predicate, the maximal pro-`p` quotient and the free pro-`p` groups will be stated against, and it already transports along continuous surjections, quotients and topological isomorphisms.

name: Cofinality of open normal subgroups
text: a closed subgroup is the infimum of its joins with the open normal subgroups, which lets arguments over open subgroups above a closed subgroup be run over normal ones.

name: Clopen images in quotients
text: the image of an open subgroup in `G ⧸ N` is clopen, the lemma behind the totally-disconnected instance.

name: Symmetric perfect Frobenius pairing

name: The MacWilliams identity
text: for a linear code `C` over a finite field with `q` elements, `#C · W_{C⊥}(X, Y) = W_C(X + (q - 1)Y, X - Y)` in `ℤ[X, Y]`, proved from a Poisson summation formula over the code; the Krawtchouk, normalized and self-dual forms follow.

name: Type II lengths are divisible by eight
text: a doubly even, Euclidean self-dual binary code has length `≡ 0 (mod 8)`, by evaluating the MacWilliams symmetry at `(1, i)` against the fourth-root-of-unity symmetry of a doubly even enumerator.

name: The extended binary Golay code
text: the row space of `[I₁₂ | B]`, with the bordered reverse-circulant block of Huffman-Pless, is a doubly even self-dual `[24, 12, 8]` code with enumerator `X^24 + 759 X^16 Y^8 + 2576 X^12 Y^12 + 759 X^8 Y^16 + Y^24`, and deleting any coordinate leaves a `[23, 12, 7]` code.

name: Type II codes over `ℤ/2^r`
text: for `r ≥ 1`, a self-orthogonal code over `ℤ/2^r` has an even unimodular Construction A lattice exactly when it is self-dual with all Euclidean weights divisible by `2^(r+1)`; at `r = 1` this is the binary Type II statement.

name: The discriminant module of Construction A is `C⊥/C`
text: for a self-orthogonal additive code over `ℤ/m`, the discriminant bilinear module of `P_m(C)` is isometric to the actual quotient `C⊥/C`, obtained from the general gluing theorem, with a quadratic version for even `m` and quadratically isotropic `C`.

name: The weight enumerator
text: `W_C(X, Y) = ∑_w A_w(C) X^(n-w) Y^w` with integer coefficients, defined for any set of words, so MacWilliams, the named-code enumerators and the Type II symmetries all concern one polynomial.

name: The Construction A lattice
text: integer vectors of `ℚ^ι` reducing into an additive code over `ℤ/m`, with the dot product divided by `m`, bundled only under self-orthogonality; every dual carrier lives in the same rational space, so `P_m(C)^∨ = P_m(C^⊥)` is a literal equality.

name: Codes as discriminant subgroups
text: reduction modulo `m` identifies the discriminant module of `mℤ^ι` with `(ℤ/m)^ι`, so an additive code pulls back to a subgroup of an actual discriminant group, where the integral-lattices gluing API applies.

name: The divisor of `dx`
text: for a separating element `x` of a field with exact constants, the Weil differential `dx` has divisor `−2 (x)_∞ + Diff(F/k(x))`, which is therefore canonical.

name: The Weierstrass equation of a genus-one field
text: at each rational place `P` of a genus-one field with exact constants, some `x` and `y` with pole divisors `2P` and `3P` satisfy a Weierstrass equation over `k` and generate the field, in the form `y² = x³ + a₂x² + a₄x + a₆` away from characteristic two.

name: Rigidity of automorphisms

name: The Hasse–Minkowski induction step in rank at least five

name: Stone's theorem

name: Bochner's theorem
